Quest_AMelodyRemebered.description: A jewellery box in Ghornfell plays a haunting melody, but it cannot complete its song.

objectives.text: The jewellery box requires a specific ring.
The jewellery box requires a specific amulet.

dialogueRefs.text: The broken melody urges you towards the music box. The contraption looks unfinished, with a round slot where an item might rest.
An ornate jewellery box, with velvet lining. There is a round indentation where an item might rest.
The jewellery box sits quietly, the velvet slot empty.
Something is inscribed on the front.
The music lingers faintly in the air. A memory of Ghornfell, long past.

"Fire burns, the great earth shakes. Water sloshes into lakes."
"Nature stitches up the seams. Law tempers its dreams."
The story has been heard, but the melody remains.
"Around them all, a single band. A twinkling star upon the hand."
Something is inscribed on the front.
Place the inspiring ring of runecrafting?
Something is inscribed on the front.
Place the amulet of magic?

"Fire burns, the great earth shakes. Water sloshes into lakes."
"Nature stitches up the seams. Law tempers its dreams."
The ring clicks into place. Something inside the box whirrs, rotates, and reveals a second slot.
The melody from the box plays on.

"Ashenfall, I must confide, that while you wait and dream and hide,"
"Uninspired magic is growing ever stronger, I fear you won't contain it any longer."
You socket the amulet into the slot.
The melody from the box plays on.
"Around them all, a single band. A twinkling star upon the hand."
There is a new inscription.
"This is the cant that I expressed, as I wore magic's eye upon my breast."
A reward is waiting for you here, but you have no space in your inventory.
A compartment opens, revealing your reward.

"Ashenfall, I must confide, that while you wait and dream and hide,"
"Uninspired magic is growing ever stronger, I fear you won't contain it any longer."
"This is the cant that I expressed, as I wore magic's eye upon my breast."
Walk away
Place amulet
Place ring
Walk away

objectives.text: Read the Advert-Inna-Bottle next to Manktongue
Discuss the advert with Manktongue
Gather an undead chicken, magnetised iron bar and undead twigs, and bring them to Manktongue
Return to Manktongue

dialogueRefs.text: Nice day fer a walk, innit?
Need help with da in-greedy-yums for the Arrow Grabber?
What can ol' Manktongue do for you?
Oi oi!
Howdy, lankylegs.
To all inventors! Rather than patent or make money from my invention - AVA'S ACCUMULATOR - I have made the decision to make it freely available.
To all inventors! Rather than patent or make money from my invention - AVA'S ACCUMULATOR - I have made the decision to make it freely available.
I like hitting fings, I do.
Wait - is that a chicken stuck to a cliff face?
The undead magnetised chicken tries to nibble your neck as you bundle it into your bag.
You would grab the undead magnetised chicken, but you have no space in your inventory.
What an odd-looking bundle of twigs.
The bundle of undead twigs moans as you stash them in your backpack.
You would pick up the bundle of undead twigs, but you have no space in your inventory.
So, full diss-closure: Manktongue got as far as findin' an undead chicken.
Magnetisin' stuff ain't that 'ard.
Advert is vague about undead twigs, right? Manktongue plan to give dat feedback to Ava when he meets her.
Oo, get you.
It part of ol' Manktongue now.
Well, it's good to see ya again.
This invention will offer a chance to recover arrows or bolts that are lost when firing a ranged weapon.
This invention will offer a chance to recover arrows or bolts that are lost when firing a ranged weapon.
I like hitting fings, I do.
'Ello hooman. Got somefin' you need whacked?
Thing is, Manktongue got da order of opper-ations wrong and axey-dentally magnetised it.
Bring five law runes and an iron bar to Pulpknuckle up da stairs and he'll do it for ya.
Only place Ol' Manktongue as seen dem is in Bloodblight Swamp. Near a tree with glowy orange stuff on it.
Go get all da in-greedy-yums mentioned in da advert, 'an bring them back to me. I'll be takin' a load off.
It comes wiv da territory. I am a pie-in-ear, af'er all.
Look me up on Link Tin.
Got a moment for ol' Manktongue?
Howdy, lankylegs.
How can ol' Manktongue 'elp?
Components:1 x Undead Chicken, 1 x Magnetised Iron Bar and 1 x Undead Twig Bundle.
Components:1 x Undead Chicken, 1 x Magnetised Iron Bar and 1 x Undead Twig Bundle.
Makin' magnets is my special-tea.
Undead chicken is headin' due north. Probby got stuck to somethin' metal. If you head north, I reckon you'll find da chicken in no time.
It's an 'orrible place. You will need to find a tree wiv glowing orange warty bits all over it.
Manktongue's got an opper-toonity for ya. It'll blow yer bronze boots off.
Oi oi! Good to see me ol' bizness partner again!
Happy building, fellow inventors! Ava
Happy building, fellow inventors! Ava
Unless it's been eaten by a Garou, and den you're looking for a magnetised, undead Garou.
Nice, nice. Here's the deal-io. Ol' Manktongue found a message in a bottle. It's an advert-eye-cement from da mainland.
Your loss, stinkum.
For whacky magnet you'll need one iron bar and five law runes.
Manktongue try to make da machine described in da advert-eye-cement, but fings not go to plan.
You have no space in your inventory.
Bish bash bosh. One extra strong magnet.
But now YOU here. And YOU be Manktongue's bizness partner. YOU help Manktongue make da machine.
You deaf or summat? Read da advert-inna-bottle next to me.
Good good. Now we can talk 'bout Ava's Accoo...
Ah, seems you've already read da advert.
You got no space,  grotface. Huh-huh, I rhymed.
Trust me. Don't eat it. Ain't worth it.
Have a look at da advert-inna-bottle next to me. Talk to me after, an' we can work out terms.
Accooma latte... Accooma llama... Accooma matata...
Good good. Now we can talk 'bout Ava's Accoo...
Oi oi! Looks like ya got all da in-greedy-yums for the Arrow Grabba. Want me to work my magic?
...Arrow grabba.
Accooma latte... Accooma llama... Accooma matata...
Okay. A little glue here. A little elbow grease there. Ta-da! Made you one Arrow grabba!
Cool beans. Let ol' Manktongue know when you ready for da next step.
This is how we gonna make da Arrow Grabba. Step one: you make da Arrow Grabba.
...Arrow grabba.
I'm gonna come clean to ya: I may have con-figgered da Arrow Grabba a tad.
Step two: profit.
This is how we gonna make da Arrow Grabba. Step one: you make da Arrow Grabba.
Some of da arrows are gonna come to ol' Manktongue. Call it da Manktongue Tax. Dat's biz-ness for ya.
Go get all da in-greedy-yums mentioned in da advert, 'an bring them back to me. I'll be takin' a load off.
Step two: profit.
But I fink you will be pleased, none-da-less.
Before ya go, do ya wanna ask ol' Manktongue anyfink?
Go get all da in-greedy-yums mentioned in da advert, 'an bring them back to me. I'll be takin' a load off.
Go forth! Fire dem arrows, grab dem arrows! And who knows? Maybe we can come to anuvver deal in the foo-ture?
Oi oi, you ain't got room for da Arrow Grabba!
Before ya go, do ya wanna ask ol' Manktongue anyfink?
Come back when you got a single space to carry it.
Isn't the pie uncomfortable?
Nothing, thanks
Not right now
Ask about Cook's Assistant
Could you smith me a magnetised iron bar?
I've got all the information I need
Ask about Undead Twig Bundle
Ask about the Undead Chicken
Ask about the Magnetised Iron Bar
Not yet
Sure
Sure
Ask about something else
Ask about Cook's Assistant
Ask about Animal Magnetism

Quest_BrinkOfExtinction.description: Help Zi to become a real KotHaar

objectives.text: Use the KotHaar numbering book to get past the KotHaar Bouncer
Bring 1 cactus steak and 3 raw beltfish back to Zi in Umbral Sands
Touch 4 pedestals in any order in THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE - 0/4
Touch 4 pedestals in any order in THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE - 1/4
Touch 4 pedestals in any order in THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE - 2/4
Return to Zi in the Burning Spire region of the Umbral Sands
Touch 4 pedestals in any order in THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE - 3/4
Use the password to enter the Cave of Screams, within the Burning Spire region
Return to the KotHaar Bouncer outside of the Cave of Screams

dialogueRefs.text: Pass, human.
Oh my, OH MY, it's a human! Look at how long and weird-looking you are! You're like half a spider.
Hello hello! Do you remember me? It's the KotHaar, Zi!
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
Unless you wish to be forged into a KotHaar, which is likely impossible, there is nothing more for you here.
None shall pass, by command of Fuzan.
You hear screams from beyond the door. Yeah, this is the Cave of Screams alright.
You step away from the door.
You pick up something small, black and buzzing with energy.
Nothing interesting happens.
I thought humans would shrivel up in the Scorch, but LOOK at you. The name is KotHaar-Hok-Zi, but you can call me Zi. And, unlike you, I...I'm not as well suited to the Scorch.
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
These are huge and... on fire. I wonder why they are here?
Halt! Speak the password to me, stranger, or you shall not pass.
Halt! This place is not for your eyes. Turn back.
Halt! Speak the password to me, stranger, or you shall not pass.
But I will say that I admire your skill, human.
OH MY KILN you were amazing! I was all like 'ARGH I AM IN THE GRIP OF FUZAN!' and you were like 'I WILL SAVE YOU, ZI!'.

It's why I am out here, actually. I was told that I couldn't be a real KotHaar, on account of my frailty. But it's only temporary! I am going to prove that I am definitely NOT the weak-link they say I am.
The KotHaar Bouncer snorts.
The KotHaar Bouncer snorts.
Hrmmm. Not quite.
Human. I despair. Remember the numbering book that I gave you?
The KotHaar Bouncer snorts.
Correct, human who is clearly not a KotHaar.
What a day, eh? Well, I guess I'm a KotHaar Core now. A tiny marble. But at least I've not being puppeted by a giant dragon, right?
OH MY KILN I just had a brilliant idea! You can teach me how to survive in the desert!
OH NO YOU DIDN'T! Calm as you like, you just sauntered over to the pedestals, touched them, and came back to me! Legend. Absolute legend.
Oh, I must admit I thought you would be completing THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE.
I see you have reversed the forging process, KotHaar-Hok-Zi.
Zi is inside. But I warn you - he is changed.
It would serve you well, human, to read the guide I gave you.
It would serve you well, human, to read the guide I gave you.
And you answered that without even reading the leaflet I gave you. Almost as if you were guided to the answer by some invisible force.
Could you do me a favour and take me to the Bouncer outside of the cave? I've got a bit of house-keeping to do.
Thank you thank you thank you. You will NOT regret this. Okay, what do survival people do in the desert? Ah, yes, they make their own food!
Of course! You are busy! Very busy! I will wait here and die and become one with the desert.
You came back! And you brought the cactus steak and the fish belts!
Did you bring me the things that you gathered from the desert?
Right, I think I've learned enough from you. I'm ready to be accepted by my people. I'm going to the Cave of Screams, to the west behind the sunken pyramid.
If you don't have time, that's fine, obviously. But if you do have time, then four thumbs up.
I did, with help from the adventurer. Um, after some consideration, I have decided that I am not going to be a KotHaar after all.
He was accepted by the KotHaar, but on one condition: his core must be forged into a new body. And that body is controlled by Fuzan.
Zi is inside. But I warn you - he is changed.
Bring me 1 cactus steak and 3 raw beltfish. Show me how to gather life from the sand like a desert witch! A sand-witch, hehe!
This is all too much. Okay, okay, next up is THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE! You're going to show me how to navigate lava and also be a kickass hero.
No? Oh - not a bother. You have so much to do, being an adventurer and all.
Come see how I do! There's a KotHaar Bouncer there, guarding the entrance. He will ask for a password.
Go out there on your magic carpet, find four pedestals that look like giant black blocks, and tag them before coming back.
The Bouncer looks from side to side, as if checking if someone is watching.
He was accepted by the KotHaar, but on one condition: his core must be forged into a new body. And that body is controlled by Fuzan.
Um, could you make some room for me to hop in your pockets? It's crowded in there.

Out there, around the Burning Spire, are four pedestals. They're giant black blocks with fire on top - you can't miss them. You are going to touch the four pedestals in any order and then come back to me.
I'll just sit here and slowly erode into nothingness.
It is SO simple. Count the total number of words that he says to you. The total number IS the password. See you in there! I'M GOING TO BE A REAL KOTHAAR!
You misunderstand, human. We do not speak numbers as you do.
Good for you, little one. Grab this opportunity with all four hands. I wish I had done the same.
Meanwhile, I'm going to shout your name and periodically punch the air!
Think like a KotHaar. Take this book and return when you can count… properly.
And you, human - you have been a friend to this little KotHaar. I wish to give you a trophy from Zi's discarded body.
Ugh. Humans and their tiny pockets. Come back when you have space for what I give you.
Or, at least, I would if you had any space in your piddling human pockets. Empty some space and come back to me.
Two triangles separated by a line?
Two crosses?
Twelve
Ten
Eleven
Twelve
Turn away
No, I don't have time for that
Enter the Cave of Screams
Yes, I suppose so?

Quest_Contact.description: Work with Avisk to find a potential shortcut to Fuzan's Volcano

objectives.text: Find the Vault Guardian Prime in the Kalphite Hive
Find 3 missing vault guardians and recover their Crystal Helix fragments
Use the Crystal Helix to pass through the magical barrier in the Kalphite Hive
Talk to Zanik in the Shortcut Chamber within the Kalphite Hive
Follow the footsteps in the sand to find who made them
Break the four crystals in the Shortcut Chamber of the Kalphite Hive
Return to the Vault Guardian Prime
Return to Zanik in the Shortcut Chamber within the Kalphite Hive
Find Crystal Helix fragments. 1/3
Find Crystal Helix fragments. 2/3

dialogueRefs.text: The vault guardian lies half-buried in the sand, its frame twisted and silent.
The vault guardian lies shattered, its frame torn apart. Deep score marks cut through the plating.
A decommissioned Vault Guardian. Very odd.
Kalphite assault… overwhelming. Game over man... Game over...
Non-designated individual detected.
Our paths cross again, mortal! I have need of someone with legs, hands and an impressionable character. While they are common evolutionary traits, I'm lacking them all here in the desert.
I suppose your mushy mortal mind has forgotten the current objective.
Going by the lack of colour in the crystal, Avisk is no longer home.
My objective is complete. I can rest now.
The core housing has been pried open. If the Crystal Helix was here, it has been taken.

Thanks for helping with that dragonkin buffoon. I slipped a dagger into the vein of consciousness within his crystal. It's only a setback for him, as he will have other crystals for his mind to retreat into.
Take the Crystal Helix fragment… Complete the task…
A wall of energy blocks the path. The air hums with power.
Avisk 0, Team Adventurers 1. We should get out of here.
It is a red crystal with a deep glow to it.
The vein within the crystal pops disgustingly.
It is a red crystal with a deep glow to it.
The vein gushes out horribly.
It is a red crystal with a deep glow to it.
The chamber shakes as you throttle the vein.
It is a red crystal with a deep glow to it.
You yank the vein out of the pedestal.
I did have some vault guardians, who had hands at least, but they seem to have expired. It's really rather irritating.
Its energy core flickers weakly. There is space for 4 vault shards in the core. Perhaps they would reactivate it?
Its energy core flickers weakly. There is space for 4 vault shards in the core. Perhaps they would reactivate it?
Carry on the mission... Use the Crystal Helix to pass through the magical barrier.
Unit damaged… systems failing…
Small footprints lead away from the ruined guardian. They look like they belong to something goblin-sized.
I was wondering when you’d show up!
You made it into the Umbral Sands! It was never in doubt. I'm a little busy now, but shall we catch up later?
Keep working on that Crystal Helix. I'm going to see if there's another way past that magical barrier.
Phew! Definitely took the harder route into this cave. Wait a minute - are those crystals the same as the one outside?
That should be it! We've undermined his plan to mind-meld with the kalphite and the Kalphite Queen. Who knows what THAT might have been like.
You can't destroy Avisk! I have many places like this - full of my consciousness.
Perhaps we could work together? You can have Ghornfell. I have no use for Ghornfell.
Must I be humiliated? Why am I always the one who is shamed?
Don't think that this is the end. We will meet again, puny human.
I want you to find my vault guardians and retrieve a Crystal Helix they were carrying. It is the key to a... shortcut which leads directly to Fuzan's Volcano.
Find my defunct vault guardians, gather fragments of the Crystal Helix, and use them together to open up a shortcut to Fuzan in the cave back there.
What are you waiting for? You have the Crystal Helix. Go into the Kalphite Hive, pass the magical barrier, and meet your doo... victory!
The vault shards magnetise into place.
The vault guardian's core flickers with what seems like sadness.
The light in its core fades.
You don't have space to take the Crystal Helix fragment.
The barrier seemed to scan you for something, then shoved you back once it found it missing.
The Crystal Helix spins brightly in your hands. The barrier shifts and matches the light of the Crystal Helix. It allows you to pass.
Avisk is everywhere, mortals! Adventurerer, complete your quest. All that remains is for you to jump into the hole with the Crystal Helix. It will take you directly to Fuzan!
All that's left is for me to deal with the giant Avisk crystal on the surface.
That interests you, yes? You want to confront Fuzan, don't you? Use the Crystal Helix to access a secret entrance in the nearby cave. Help me and we both benefit.
Auxiliary power… restored…
Crystal Helix fragments detected. You carry them, Vault Guardian Prime.
Ah, you found the dismembered vault guardian? Yeah, that was my handiwork. In fact, it's something I would like to discuss...
It is incredibly good to see you, but we have a problem - a problem we need to align on.
Ha! Like we'd believe that, you goofy carbon deposit! Notice how there's heat coming from the hole? Avisk must want the Crystal Helix melted in the lava or geyser that lies down there.
Here, have a reward for trusting me over that fancy pebble. I found it in a tunnel that led into this cave. Looks impressive.
Crystal Helix... fragment… released…
Non-designated individual detected. Access denied.
Deliver fragments to this unit. Unit will then repair the Crystal Helix.
You seem to be helping Avisk, but you're too clever to REALLY be helping Avisk. You have an angle on this, don't you?
Of course! Avisk wants to diffuse his consciousness to the kalphite and the Kalphite Queen! In what world was that plan going to work, Avisk?
Crystal Helix remains incomplete.
Protocol override. Vault Guardian Prime status will be conferred to new subject. YOU are now Vault Guardian Prime.
Reconstruction complete. Mission… fulfilled.
Fragments withheld. Directive cannot be fulfilled. Return when ready.
Ooh, very clandestine! Keep your friends close and your enemies closer, right? Close enough to put them in a headlock.
You better believe something is off! Avisk has zero interest in finding a shortcut to Fuzan. It's a big old stinking ruse.
Don't listen to the goblin! Jump into the hole like a good mortal!
Er, could you clear out some of the stuff in your inventory? I can't give you the reward with so much in there.
You don't have space to take the Crystal Helix fragment.
One lies buried… outside... within a ruin of some kind.
Mission handover: the Crystal Helix was… shattered into three fragments.
I'd like to suggest an alternative plan. You complete the Crystal Helix, then we access this Shortcut Chamber - whatever it is - and then we undermine whatever Avisk's REAL plan is.
Pffrt. What do you say we play a bit of whack-a-crystal? Get your pickaxe out.
One was captured... in this cave. An obstruction pins the unit in place.
Three vault guardians are in possession of them. Recover the fragments… and this unit can restore the Crystal Helix. Then... magical barrier will open.
How does that sound? If you're in, you will be needing this...
The last rests near some eggs of the kalphite... on the surface...
Or, at least, you would if you had space. Make some room and then we can go undercover.
Hand over Crystal Helix fragments
Walk away
I thought something was off...
Place 4 vault shards into the core
Walk away
I'm working against him

Quest_CooksAssistant.description: Help Slopfinger in Ghornfell bake a memorable cake for Manktongue.

objectives.text: Gather 4 eggs, 6 wheat and a bucket of milk, and bring them all to Slopfinger.
Bake a cake using the stove next to Slopfinger.
Bring the signed cake to Manktongue.
Show Slopfinger the freshly cooked cake.
Give Slopfinger the good news.

dialogueRefs.text: The Dairy Cow gives you the side-eye.
Need any help with da stuff?
That's certainly a stove.
Blimey, I seen a lot of hoomans, but ain't you a big 'un?
Howdy, lankylegs.
Much obliged for yer 'elp.
The Dairy Cow gives you the side-eye.
The cow looks supremely confident within its own body. It's to be admired, really.
The Dairy Cow permits you to milk her.
Chicken or terrorbird eggs will do. We don't need to get too fancy.
It's not my for-tay, but I believe it involves farmin'.
You'll need to milk a Dairy Cow. I don't advise milkin' anything else.
We all need help. But you work that out for yoursel'.
Tell 'Slopfinger he's earned himself a raise.
You given Slopfinger da news about da raise?
Name is Slopfinger. I work for Manktongue ova there. I'm his cook, assistant, butler, mass-ooze and hype-goblin.
The cow turns its head expectedly.
The Dairy Cow gives you a kick to the shins.
The cow rolls its eyes but blushes a little.
It's smooth, like a wide, hornless unicorn.
The Dairy Cow notes that you have no inventory space and rolls her eyes. You will need to come back when you have room for a bucket of milk.
I'll want four of da blighters, so that the cake will rise as high as my blood pressure.
Find some wheat seeds and a farmin' patch, and do whatever it is that farmers do. Remember, we need 6 lots of wheat.
Findin' a dairy cow is the problem. Not so many of them round Ghornfell.
See ya later.
Slopfinger said that I need 4 eggs, 6 wheat and a bucket of milk to bake the cake.
Hop to it! Fortune waits for no gobber.
Not that he notices me. Yesterday I was crackin' 'is back an' he called me Sweatmonger. Sweatmonger!
You have no wheat to feed the cow.
The Dairy Cow chews the wheat without once taking its eyes off you.
You won't need to make flour or anythin'. I like my cakes to look like sad bread.
Is it? Blimey - I thought it were a bear.
Go away. I gots nothin for yas.
If only I could think of a way to get Manktongue to remember my name...
Go give da cake to Manktongue.
I saw the cake go in his lughole! What did he say?
That cake is ace. Truly ace.
I've been trying not to maintain eye contact. Been on edge the whole day.
Do you want to put the ingredients inside the stove?
Oi oi, what do we have 'ere?
Oi oi! You got somethin' for ol' Manktongue?
You know what, I utterly forgot that I'm a cook! Yer a genie-ooze.
What a ruddy charmer! He even remembered ma name!
Now, don't look for a moment. I need to apply my sig-nah-ture.
You close your eyes,  jumble the ingredients together, and place them in the stove. Surely this won't work.
You step back from the stove.
Wait, wot's written on da cake? Does that say Slopfinger? Da goblin in da kitchen?
Da cake is a lie! Hehe.
You shall be the assistant's assistant. We will need 4 eggs, 6 lots of wheat and a bucket of milk.
I feel a growin' pride in the work I do. I cannot fank you enough.
The spit will show up well on da frostin'. Now hurry, give the cake to Manktongue.
...It worked.
Give ol' Manktongue a moment.
Well, come back over when you've made a new 'un.
If you need any 'elp wiv finding any of it, ya know where I am.
It ain't much, but I want ya to 'ave this. Perhaps, one day, you will find a boss as good as Manktongue.
I'll be back here with my heart fully in ma mouth.
I can tell from the way you're walkin' that you've got bakery stuffs for me.
Manktongue pushes some cake into his ear, where it nestles next to the pie.
It's a talent. It can't be taught.
Ooh, the icin' is drip-droppin' on ma eardrum.
Next step is to make the cake. You look like ya know yer way 'round a stove. Why don't you have a go?
Tell 'Slopfinger he's earned himself a raise.
Goodness no! My hands are all wobbly at the thought of Manktongue learnin' ma name.
Why not bake him a cake with your name on it?
Let's bake!
Milk it
It's a cake, made for you by Slopfinger
I don't need help
Tell her 'you're udderly gorgeous'
Isn't that a Dairy Cow over there?
Shouldn't you be making it?
Did you just write your name in spit?
He said, and I quote: "tell Slopfinger he's earned himself a raise".
I had a cake, but I lost it.
Ask about a bucket of milk
Ask about wheat
Ask about eggs
That's oddly poetic
Pet it
Walk away
Feed it some wheat

Quest_DR_FTUE_Fishing.description: The Wise Old Man has some tips on how to grow as an amateur angler.

objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man to learn about Fishing.
Fish a Sardine at a fishing spot near the Wise Old Man.
Return to the Wise Old Man.

dialogueRefs.text: Anything else I can help you with?
Ah, wonderful, a delicious sardine. It brings back old memories. Now I just need to fry it up, just like old grampa used to. Thank you, adventurer. Here, for your troubles.

Aha, a very useful tool you've managed to make for yourself, there. Why, I remember in my, admittedly distant, youth, spending countless hours trying to catch something from a local pond with one. The owners were not happy.
Still looking for fish? I have a few tips that might help.

It is the simplest thing in the world. Just equip your net in your hands, stand inside of the Net Fishing Spot and start trawling. The small fish are hidden away, among all types of junk, so don't be discouraged.
Oh, now those are interesting. You see, each fish has different tastes, and if you have a bait a fish likes equipped while fishing, you get a better chance of catching them.

That’s where it gets interesting. Fish don’t exactly want to be caught, so they will put up a fight! Once one bites, it’ll try to bolt and you'll need to wear it out. Move from side to side to counter the direction it’s swimming in and keep the pressure on.
They say fish based food is the best way to restore your lost health! Definitely worth the effort to catch and cook them!

Why, if you can find yourself a nice spot, it can be a relaxing way to wile away the dull daylight hours between adventures -- challenging yourself to find that one, pristine, fish you see mockingly swimming in the waters before you.
The more you practice the easier it will become to catch something. Stronger fish require stronger nets, so remember to upgrade!
Some fish like eating other, smaller, fish - the sort you can find with your net. Others prefer a moving target, and jingly things like feathers draw their attention.

Do it long enough and the fish will become exhausted for a short time, that’s your cue to reel it in! Just keep an eye on your stamina and don’t get sloppy, or you’ll snap the line and watch your prize swim away.

Boil them, roast them, put them in a stew. You can make all sorts of delicious dishes from all sorts of fishes. Oh and if you find some really nice ones, you can put them on display if you want to show off your angling skills.

Ah, but I haven't eaten a good fish for ages! Hrmm... how about you look around and see if you could find me a sardine in the waters around here. You'll need a Fishing Rod to catch one though! You may want to consider crafting some bait too!
What can I do with the fish?
Can you tell me about fishing with nets?
Can you tell me about rod fishing?
Can you tell me about bait?

progressionTriggers.unlockQueryString: ANY ITEMS[ Coarse Net, Fine Net, Mystic Net, Wool Net, Ash Rod, Maple Rod, Oak Rod, Willow Rod ]

dialogueRefs.text: Forgive me, but I must focus my attention elsewhere. There is an enormous backlog in Fellhollow that I need to clear up.
Here let me take that dragon head from you.
Hrmm, you appear to be a little overburdened. Shed yourself some of thy worldly trappings and then come speak to me again.
A foul thing, really. Corrupted beyond repair. I almost pity her. Still, you're not interested in that, I feel you'll enjoy this much more.
You did well here, in Fellhollow, but there is yet more for you to do. A, shall we say, colleague of mine awaits your help in the Umbral Sands.
Now, I have an enormously unpleasant cleanup to do. So you'll forgive me if I get back to work.
I have sent young Cathan ahead to gather allies and investigate. You should find him to the east of Fellhollow.
While you're around and if you have time to spare - which you do, I've checked my list - go and speak to Postie Pete. He has something he could use your help with.
Now that the Gatekeeper is gone, the way to the Umbral Sands is open. We'll meet you there, just got a few things to finish up here.
Nasty place this, ain't it? Crazed black knights, somehow still around even though it looks like they should have all died long ago
Hrmm?
Nasty place this, ain't it? Crazed black knights, somehow still around even though it looks like they should have all died long ago
Problem being, we're stuck in this place until we can get this ruddy door open. It's barring our way to the desert, and nothing I try seems to fix it.
Problem being, we're stuck in this place until we can get this ruddy door open. It's barring our way to the desert, and nothing I try seems to fix it.
Hrmm?
As far as I can tell, it's all connected to that great big stone over there. Seems like some sort of mystical doohicky that powers it all.
As far as I can tell, it's all connected to that great big stone over there. Seems like some sort of mystical doohicky that powers it all.
It's broken currently, a few pieces missing. I figure if we repair it, we might get that barrier open. Go give the stone a look will you? See what it needs to get it fixed.
It's broken currently, a few pieces missing. I figure if we repair it, we might get that barrier open. Go give the stone a look will you? See what it needs to get it fixed.
An ancient dragonkin brain in a rock, eh? Weird choice, but to each their own I guess. Well, the barrier's down now, but there's something big and dangerous beyond. Your area I think.
We can't get through to the desert unless we can open this barrier. It seems to be connected to that stone over there, see if you can find all the pieces of it, would you?
Looks like you're making some headway on those shards, keep it going. When it's repaired, hopefully that crystal will tell us how to get this barrier open.
You've got them all! Wonderful! Best go fix up that big, weird, stone and see if we can get this barrier open.
Hrmm?
[Ask About What's Theirs is Mine]
[Ask About What's Theirs is Mine]
[Ask About Black Knight's Fortress]
[Ask About What's Theirs is Mine]
There, now, the gate's open and you're free to go. Nay, I'd say you're encouraged to go.
...broken...shards...self...missing...
...find...pieces...shards...lost...me...whole...
...broken...shards...self...missing...
I've unlocked the barrier for you. You'll just have to get rid of that great big gatekeeper. Unless you want to surrender your mind to me so that I may do it and then walk this world as a living god?

Oh, you slew the titan? I am impressed. Really you are quite capable, aren't you? When I find myself a new body and walk the world as a living god, you should come work for me. We'll do great things together!
Rivalry... betrayal... hatred.
A grand project of cooperation, crafted by a society of paranoid narcissists.
Broken... shattered... lost.
I am a voice without a name, howling in the wilderness of memory.
Memories... anger... death.
Once a man, but now no longer. Three minds rage within a twisted form.
...seek around keep...I grant...authorisation...
...I am... I remember... broken... lost...
Pieces of me, falling into place... a name on the edge of memory...
I am nearly whole...I walked the world, striding above it and overseeing everything... I was in a desert, sand beneath my feet and knowledge all around me...
I am restored!
...find...pieces...shards...lost...me...whole...
No? Fair, worth a shot.
There, now, the gate's open and you're free to go. Nay, I'd say you're encouraged to go.
They sought power over others and soon power over one another. Reaching across worlds without the knowledge to control what lay beyond.
They called themselves the Children of Shadows, though sometimes Darkness, they wanted to be seen as sinister secretive masters.  A society of chaos and rebellion, if you can imagine such a thing.
I was not always this. Once I walked these lands, towering above it.
Many of your lifetimes ago, I walked this realm safe in the knowledge that there were none who could harm me. I was a scientist, a scholar, a genius dragged down by weaker minds.
A great giant of a man, a titan one might say. Flesh twisted, mind shattered, but far more deadly than before.

Lord Rasmodel waits beyond that barrier, though he is not as he was. The energies he absorbed from my shattering, as well as that cthonian's parasitic cells have transformed him into something different.

The stone appears to be shattered, with large pieces missing from it as if struck at a single point with a large, blunt, instrument. You believe it would be easy to repair if you found all the pieces.
Yet, I cannot remember all... I must... you must... the last pieces, return them to me. Make me whole once more and I can aid you in your quest.

Mwaha, mwahaha, mwahahahaha! Foolish little mammal, so simple in your thoughts that you cannot even grasp the depths of my genius. My name, it would rattle around in your tiny skull like the echoes within a cave.
...seek around keep...I grant...authorisation...
Please... please go, and take your hammer with you. Here, a little bribe so that you and your hammer get very far away from me.
More than was bargained for lay beyond the gate. It would lead to their undoing.
Some sought martial expertise, others delved into arcane knowledge and secrets that the rest of your kind foolishly abhor. It was these who found me buried in the sand of the desert, biding my time.
Bound into stone, so that I might escape some dread nightmare.
Until the creation of one of my small-minded colleagues grew too arrogant and thought to strike down her masters.
A great giant of a man, a titan one might say. Flesh twisted, mind shattered, but far more deadly than before.
Tremble, ignorant creature and marvel in my majesty! For I am Avisk the eternal, the greatest mind to ever grace the Aughra! Now, you will submit to me and become my thrall so that together we may...

Soon distrust began to brew among the humans. I had some small part to play in that. Boredom is a poison no one can resist, and the antidote showed itself in small amusements. A whisper here, a secret there, and soon they turned on each other without mercy.
Now, I am lost and broken. Just shadows on the wall.

While the others died, or cowered in fear waiting for their destruction, I preserved my intellect within this very stone. My knowledge, my genius, my... what you call soul... would live forever enshrined in glittering stone.
A fragment of myself drives him, separate from the mind that speaks to you now. In a strange way, like the knights of this place, I am in a civil war of myself.
Why are you looking at me like that?
Oh, you're hands are full... I do somewhat miss hands... anyway, come back and see me when you've got some space free for my little gift. .
They summoned demons. They trained armies and all the while they unsheathed their knifes and looked to one another.

While the others died, or cowered in fear waiting for their destruction, I preserved my intellect within this very stone. My knowledge, my genius, my... what you call soul... would live forever enshrined in glittering stone.
But the voice that speaks to you now, know that it is far more your ally than the beast beyond that barrier. At least a voice of crystal, you can trust.
In time their rivalries turned into open conflict and that damned fool, Rasmodel, turned his blade upon myself and shattered the Dreaming Stone.

One day, perhaps, I shall be freed from this prismatic prison, so that I might share my vast wisdom with the lesser beings of this world. Yet, I am not whole enough yet to do so, and more pieces of me remain.

I am unsure of what happened next, but the powers involved, the sheer magic at work... it had a terrible effect on this fortress. Those who dwelled within became twisted and strange. Life prolonged, but cursed with madness.
Hrmm... yes... well... your logic is sound. Perhaps I was a little overzealous in my bluster. Happens when you've been alone in the psyche of deranged black knights for too long.
It has been fascinating to watch.
I blame the cthonian, horrible things. Anyway, you wanted that barrier lowered? it's no trouble, just let me fiddle a few things and... yep, there you go. No hard feelings eh?

Just... be wary of Lord Rasmodel out there. Had a bit of a mishap when he smashed me to pieces and now he's got some of me, some of a demon and a whole lot of anger issues. Best give him a swift death if you ask me.
What's behind that barrier?
What are you?
What happened here?
I can just smash the crystal again
I have a hammer and I'm not afraid to use it
A powerful force holds this door shut. A chill runs down your spine reminding you that Death has a job for you and it's a good idea not to forget about it.
[PH] It's too dangerous to pick this up now.
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
There is nothing of interest
The door will not open... for now.
The barrier is solid and impassable, you will need to find some way to pass through it.
What little sanity I cling to is eroded each day I have to speak to those vile creatures. Those goblins.
Ah, delightful, a human not driven mad by the strange afflictions of this place. Delighted, delighted to meet you, truly.
Go away. I gots nothin for yas.
They can be given simple tasks, and excel at anything that involves blind violence, but anything that requires finesse appears woefully beyond them.
Ah, yes, forgive my loquaciousness, you do seem frightfully busy. I deduce from your bearing that you require the shards of the Dreaming Stone.
Eh? Wat? Wat you want? Go away, I'm trying to lick all the syrup off me nose and there's an awful lot of nose.
Hrmm, you want the besterest recipe? Is secret. I won'ts tells ya nothin unless ya gives da password.

There is one of them, the disgustingly named "Snotpit", who has taken it upon himself to guard my secrets and refuses to give them to me unless I utter the password. The password, of course, is to simply say "please".
As it happens I have one with me - indeed it is the reason for a vocabulary far removed from the rest of my kin. Intellect is a terrible curse, however, and I would sooner remove it then keep it.
One of my kindred guards a recipe that I would like to try before I give you the shard. He can be found in the shed near the waterfall, guarded by a zogre.
I won'ts tells ya nothin unless ya gives da password.
Go away. I gots nothin for yas.

Politeness, an alien concept to these foul beasts.
Still, they are better companions than the mould on the wall. It whispers strange new recipes to me that are alien and strange, both toxic and delicious. I must listen closer, or I might just go mad.
But to do so, one must first savour a last meal while I have the capacity to do so. Snotpit, a most obnoxious lout, guards a recipe in a shed by the waterfall, near a zogre's stomping ground.
Ah, yes, there it is. The sweet smell of succulent maple, autumnal molasses encased in delicious crisp bread. Oh, yes, this is worth losing my intellect for. May I?
Ah, he has given you the recipe for the most sublime of feasts - the Maple Toastie. Please, if you would make one for me, why it would be the most exquisite thing!
Nope, that's not the password. Get lost! No password, no food!
Oh! You do know password. Ok, fair enough. Here, the recipe you was lookin' for.
I yearn to taste of it. If you find the recipe, and bring me that forbidden dish, then the shard will be yours and I can return myself to a state more becoming of my nature.
Exquisite! Truly a festival of flavour. How it tickles the tongue and delights the taste buds. Yes, yes, it's truly magnificent.
Old chef know password. But he been hidden up in the tower, behind you, for ages now. Hope he comes soon, I needs the loo... though I don't know where one is...
Here, the shard, as promised. It has been a most delightful experience meeting you. I wish you well in all your adventures.
Bibbly bobbly slimey wimey?
Give it or I'll hit you?
Peekaboo?
Please?
It not workin! This rod must be broken! I stab and stab and stab and still no fish!
You could try and grab a fish, but you're carrying too much right now.
You! You're a human... I think. Might be an elf? I dunno, all pink and wobbly the lot of you. You know how this thing works, yeah? You get me fish!
Go away, you're scarin' off the fishes!
With much effort, you are able to reach in and grab a fish with your bare hands. It occurs to you that there must be a better way to do this and you start to think about how.
The fish are wise to your tactics and you'll not be able to grab them by hand again. You'll need to think up some new method of... fishing...
I want that fish! You sees it? The weird one, swimming around looking all strange and stuff. I bet it tastes delicious! Get me it and I'll give you something, fair trade, yeah?
I want that fish! You sees it? The weird one, swimming around looking all strange and stuff. I bet it tastes delicious! Get me it and I'll give you something, fair trade, yeah?
You gots it! Gimme, I been looking forward to eating this!
Blerg! This horrible and hard, like eating a rock... wait... that IS a rock! Why would fish be eating weird shiny rock? Blerg!
Ere, you have it. I don't want it and I did promise you a reward. Don't say I ain't a goblin of me word!
A mechanism clicks, as if a key has been turned in a lock.
A mechanism whirs angrily into life, resetting your progress.

There are those who say that knowledge has power, but they are only half right. Knowledge only has power if that knowledge has purpose. 
The right facts applied the right way, can change the destiny of a nation far more than the facts on their own are able.
A mechanism clicks, as if a key has been turned in a lock.
A mechanism whirs angrily into life, resetting your progress.
A mechanism clicks, as if a key has been turned in a lock.
A mechanism whirs angrily into life, resetting your progress.
A mechanism clicks, as if a key has been turned in a lock.
A mechanism whirs angrily into life, resetting your progress.
In that regard, knowledge is a key to power. Learn this well acolyte and you may begin to understand the depths of your ignorance and take the first steps to unshackle yourself from its chains.
An ancient spell, enforced by some mechanism, prevents further access. You will need to find some way to unlock it.
A mechanism whirs into life, directing arcane energies toward the centre of the library. The barrier over the door fades away.
One must first, understand that to obtain real knowledge, know that you know nothing.
One must seek knowledge, striving towards a great comprehension of the true nature of the world.
One must have ambition also. For what is power without purpose? A liability. A chain. A noose. Power must be put to task, or it is mere languid possibility, that none should seek.

Finally, one must understand the purpose of power is not to control others, but to set oneself free. For what greater rebellion is there, than knowing you walk a path entirely of your own construction?
Learn these lessons, acolyte, and perhaps you will be worthy of my attention.
Hrmm?

Well, glad to hear that the titan is dealt with. Nasty piece of work. Doric says he can get the door unstuck any day now, letting us into the desert. Locals called it the Umbral Sands... sounds creepy.
That's the question, isn't it? They should all be dead really, especially after Fellhollow, but here they are.

Back on the mainland they'd be called the Kinshra, or black knights, but this is a different order. The Kinshra were formed sometime in the early fifth age, but it looks like these weirdos might be a bit older than that.
Ah, the god of chaos, or rebellion if you're a more generous sort. He was once one of the Mahjarrat, a cruel race of shapeshifting sorcerers from the world of Freneskae.
What little research I have managed so far indicates that this place was known as Dowdun Reach.
Ah, you're here, good. Looks like you had an easier time getting here than we did. Troublesome people here, had to give a few of them quite a wallop.
Don't mind me, just dealing with some shennanigans from a talking crystal that is definitely not sinister, honest. Best get back to it I suppose.
Go speak to Doric, who's working on a solution. You can find him up in the Nexus of this place. Though you might want to set up a basecamp here first.
A black knight titan... made from the fusion of demonic sorcery, cthonian nonsense and dragonkin mad science...
Though I wouldn't exactly call this living. It seems they've become twisted, corrupted somehow, into something not entirely human.
They're Zamorak worshippers. Followers of the god of chaos. Utter nonsense really. Just a bunch of selfish idiots who want an excuse to be bullies and dabble in sinister magic, that sort of thing.
He came into power when he attempted to kill Zaros, in the second age, and stole as much of his power as he could. Zaros survived, sort of, but that's beside the point.

A group of human settlers moved here from Fellhollow some time before... well... before it all turned spooky and weird. They called themselves the Children of Shadows, because everyone wants to be edgy.
I had hoped to be hunting down the next dragon, try and whittle down Kuldra's forces. But, wouldn't you know it, there's a whole ruddy keep in the way. Full of angry Zamorakians.
Do you know, I really miss the old days when things were normal. Just give me a dragon I can hit and call it day, none of this nightmare amalgam poppcock!

There's no reasoning with them. They're each completely off their rocker and very violent about it too. I had to blast three of them earlier, when I was eating a sandwich. Terribly rude of them, really.

Ever since then Zamorak set himself up as public enemy number one to any sapient being with half a braincell. He was one of the most active combatants in the God Wars and has continued to be the source of most problems ever since.
I think they wanted this to be some bastion of chaos. A sanctuary for Zamorak worshipers, where they could be as evil as they wanted - or pretended - to be, without upsetting the locals.
Quite the bother. Good thing you're here though, you can get us moving again. The way is blocked by something called the Gatekeeper. Not sure what it is, or who it is, but it's in the way.
Anyway, best go kill it before it gets loose and learns to sail back to the mainland to upend society. You know, like these things do.
Recently he returned to Gielinor, while Guthix's edicts were down, and made a right mess of things. Adventurers had to kick him back to Infernus and recreate the Edicts so that he couldn't come back.

There's a nasty magical barrier before we can even reach them, but Doric's working on it as we speak. You can find him up in the Nexus of this place. Though you might want to set up a basecamp here first.
Good riddance I say.
What is this place?
Who is Zamorak?
Who are the Black Knights?
What happened here?
She whispers, do you hear her? For an eternity she crawls round and round inside my mind fighting with the other voice, the two of them at each other's throats.
You find a small glass owl, wrapped carefully in red cloth to protect it from the elements.
The chest is empty save for one confused spider trying to make itself a new home. You lock eyes, but say nothing to one another. Strangers passing by.
They steal memories too. How dare they! But I hid mine! Sealed it in glass. Hoot hoot! Memories safe, happiness encased in translucent gleam!
Whispering whispering, crawling round my head. I sealed them in the glittering prison, yet they skitter and jitter so.
You! Apprentice! Acolyte? Silent shadow whose soul does not scream. Find my glittering memory. Glass winged hunter of the night. Bring it me, let me smile again?
A memory in glass. A smile in kaleidoscopic fragments. Abraxus always was an artist at heart.
You! Apprentice! Acolyte? Silent shadow whose soul does not scream. Find my glittering memory. Glass winged hunter of the night. Bring it me, let me smile again?
Perhaps I am looking in the wrong places. Scratching the itch outside, rather than within? A knife to the skull, perhaps, cut the rot out from within?
I left my memories in a tranquil place, buried in the dirt. A garden where all the keep's creatures used to live. A dragon guards it now, though they know not what it is they protect.
Thank you, apprentice. Here, take this bauble as payment. But beware, it whispers in the dark!
I left my memories in a tranquil place, buried in the dirt. A garden where all the keep's creatures used to live. A dragon guards it now, though they know not what it is they protect.
Black knight titans and weird demonic curses. Ashenfall really doesn't seem to catch a break, does it?
Hello there, adventurer!
Never ends, does it? I've been investigating this place, seems to lead to some great fortress or other. It's blocking access to the Umbral Sands.
The Wise Old Man's headed further into this area, something about dark powers and such stuff.
I was gonna scout it out, spooky like, but I made the mistake of mentioning it to the Wise Old Man and... well... you know what he's like.
Knowing him, he'll have set himself up somewhere important, like a nexus type spot. You should head in and try to find him.
Said something about "rubbish defences" or "amateur hour wards" and stormed off down this passage to who knows where.
Probably want to go after him? Most likely he'll set himself up somewhere central, like a nexus or something, see if you can find it.
I'd be very happy if you could travel to Alcarrid, my camp in the south-east. It was my job to bring an envoy from other regions.
I don't know much about humans, but you don't look like a Black Knight. I guess I'll give the prepared speech anyway.
I'd be very happy if you could travel to Alcarrid, my camp in the south-east. It was my job to bring an envoy from other regions.
I COME HERE ON BEHALF OF THE MOON GAROU OF ALCARRID. WE SEEK AN ALLIANCE AGAINST THE DRAGON FUZAN.
So, not-a-Black-Knight, are you going to help us?
Well, that went better than I expected. You will need to travel south-east to Alcarrid, our camp, where your alliance will be processed.
That's...unfortunate. If and when you change your mind, come to my camp in Alcarrid and talk to the Elder.
And stay in the shadows as much as you can. The Umbral Sands is plagued by something called Scorch. The sun gives no leeway to unprepared humans.
I'm busy, I'm afraid
Sure, I will help you

Quest_DeathQuestMain.description: Put an end to the horror of Fellhollow, by defeating Imaru, the soul-devourer.

dialogueRefs.text: Cathan's dead? To shreds you say? Poor lad, not the end he deserved. But Velgar's made a mistake here, he's made this personal.
There is an indention in the altar where something would be placed. It looks like it would fit the shape of Cathan's summoning horn design.
What's that? Velgar's dead? Are you sure? I'll need to see his head, dragons can be tricky like that.
The dragon's dead, that's quite the victory. No, really, you should be proud of yourself!
I generally discourage violence, but this time I think you need to gather as much of it as possible and serve up a dragon sized portion.
There is an indention in the altar where something would be placed. It looks like it would fit the shape of Cathan's summoning horn design.
There is an indentation in the altar where something would be placed, but you are not sure what it might be.
Bring me his head and I'll make sure you're rewarded.
It's not every day you take out a draconic general infused with the elemental power of the earth. But you managed it, well done!
Build the horn. Summon Velgar. Avenge Cathan, save us all. Punch a dragon in the face!
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.

Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know. There's a strange door to the north, just past Ashien's Watch and it's sending chills down my spine. Meet me there, we'll talk more.
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Place the horn and summon Velgar>
<Step away from the altar>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>
Hrmm?
Ah, hello there.
Aren't you helping the others out? What are you talking to me for? Check your map if you're not sure what you're meant to be doing.
You've dealt with the problem for now, but who knows what danger waits around the corner? If I were you, I'd get yourself ready for whatever horribleness is coming next.
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.

Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know. There's a strange door to the north, just past Ashien's Watch and it's sending chills down my spine. Meet me there, we'll talk more.
Ask about fishing.
Ask about Farming
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>
Ask about fishing.
Ask about Farming
Is there anything I can help with?
Ask about the Dragon Slayer quest.
Oh, cease your cowering, you're not dead. You still have at least twenty minutes before I reap your soul.

I need you to investigate Fellhollow. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

Haha, just a little joke... Mostly. You'll probably die a few times, but I'll bring you back like I have been doing. I still have work for you after all. I know why you're here, little bit of a problem with the dead not actually dying.

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.

Thought I'd do some exploring, it gets boring sitting in a ruined little village all the time... so I found a new ruined area, but this time with angry dog-people. Anyway, they leave me alone, I leave them alone.

Welcome to Fellhollow. The whole region is infected with a terrible withering. Some dread curse that untethers the soul and drags it to the river Noumenon without ever sailing upon it, preventing the dead from moving on. This cannot stand.
I don't know what you're talking to me for. Aren't you busy doing stuff through that creepy door down this tunnel? Go on, get!
Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know.
The thing that really interests me though is down this little passageway. There's a door, and it's sealed by magic. Strange stuff too, old and powerful. It'll take me some time to work it out.

I need you to investigate this. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

See this creepy little passageway? There's a door at the bottom wreathed in magic, and the spooky stuff at that -- necromancy. I've been studying it for a while and I've learned the words to allow access.
But, anyway, aren't you busy? Shouldn't you be off looking at how best to stab old Velgar to death? Feels like you should be focusing your attention on that, hrmm? Go on, get!
The dragon's dead, that's quite the victory. No, really, you should be proud of yourself!

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.
Obviously, I'm not going to open it, so I'm giving the words to you. You need to go up to the door and say "Mors, introitum quaero!" and it should let you in.
It's not every day you take out a draconic general infused with the elemental power of the earth. But you managed it, well done!
Well? Go on, get! I don't have all day to hold your hand. There's something weird and sinister, go poke it with a stick like you always do!
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>

I need you to investigate Fellhollow. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.
No. You can't outrun death, no matter how hard you try. Come back and speak to me, or you're not going to get very far.
Hrmm, what are you doing here? Shouldn't you be investigating Fellhollow?

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.

There was a village once, west of the tower, that I made my home. The people lived together, peacefully, happily, under the guardianship of dragons. Imaru's grief and rage has made it a prison, all joy turned to fear. I placed a piece of the curse within its heart, an anchor made of suffering.

To the east stands a fortress that once housed the Wild Knights, brave soldiers of Guthix. They fought bravely against the endless hordes of the dead, but, like all things, fell in the end. I have left a shard of the curse there, guarded by their last living protector.

The dragonkin knew cruelty well, creating creatures whose lives were songs of suffering. Beneath the remains of Imaru's lover, behind a waterfall tainted by her sorrow, lies an ancient structure. Within it I hid a piece of the curse, guarded by the cruel masters that chained her.

I need you to investigate Fellhollow. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.

Good. I can feel the necromantic energy fluctuating, Once you've empowered yourself at all three seals then you should be able to face Imaru in her tower. Then you can put an end to her suffering, and start Fellhollow back on the slow path to healing.

Good. I can feel the necromantic energy fluctuating, Once you've empowered yourself at all three seals then you should be able to face Imaru in her tower. Then you can put an end to her suffering, and start Fellhollow back on the slow path to healing.
Good, you understand the situation now. Imaru, a soul-devouring dragon, cursed with an unending hunger and afflicted with an eternal rage. Not a good combination.
You already have this shard of the curse, there is nothing more to do here .
You already have this shard of the curse, there is nothing more to do here .
You already have this shard of the curse, there is nothing more to do here .
Yes, I already knew, but, as per my writing group, I feel showing is often better than telling. You've now seen the state of Fellhollow for yourself, it's not a good sight I'm sure you'll agree.
Grief, sorrow and fear unravel at your fingertips. A curse woven from the despair of the villagers finally stills. You take a piece of that sorrow for yourself.
A terrible despair works its way into your bones, making you shiver from the coldness of it all. As you take the power for yourself some warmth returns.
Rage unlike any other, fueled by grief and terrible loss, wraps around your heart like a vice, before its grip finally relents as you take a piece of the curse for yourself.
Those wandering dead are stuck. Trapped. Unable to move on whilst Imaru still guards the region. Furthermore, you cannot just destroy Imaru, because she is empowered by a foolish necromantic curse.

Fortunately, curses like this can be modified. They're not the more fairytale affair, none of that true love nonsense. Instead there will be a number of seals, special shrines dedicated to holding onto some aspect of the curse. You can take a piece of the curse for yourself, from each of these shrines. Get enough of them and you'll be strong enough to challenge Imaru directly.

I feel sorry for her. This was not her fault, nor her fate, but the world is cruel and there is no way to undo what was done without her destruction. So gear up, get yourself cursed, and take her down.
Grief, sorrow and fear unravel at your fingertips. A curse woven from the despair of the villagers finally stills. You take a piece of that sorrow for yourself.

A terrible despair works its way into your bones, making you shiver from the coldness of it all. As you take the power for yourself some warmth returns.

You feel the curse begin to build within you. Two shards still remain.
You feel the curse begin to build within you. Two shards still remain.
You feel the curse begin to build within you. Two shards still remain.
The curse echoes within your soul. One curse shard remains.

Your soul resonates with Imaru's grief. You are ready to bring the fight to her.
Your soul resonates with Imaru's grief. You are ready to bring the fight to her.
Your soul resonates with Imaru's grief. You are ready to bring the fight to her.

Now that you're borrowing the power of her curse, Imaru is finally vulnerable. She's had centuries of souls to feast on, and she's still one of Kuldra's draconic generals, so she won't go down easily. Make sure you're prepared.
Imaru the devourer is dead. Good! She was a potential problem that I did not want to have to deal with. You've done well, adventurer, better than the last few I sent anyway.
The door refuses to open. Powerful necromantic seals bar your entry. You will need the full power of Imaru's curse to break through them.
Unleash the curse, destroying the fragments, and face Imaru?
When she's slain, bring me her head. Gruesome, I know, but I will need it to give her spirit peace at least. Also it helps with the paperwork.
I knew one of you would luck out eventually, I'm glad it was you. Oh, yes, sorry, no chosen ones here. But ignore that, you did good, better than the rest, so you deserve what you came for.
Here let me take that dragon head from you.
If you bring me her head, then I'll turn it into something useful. Grim, yes, but one must have something to put in the filing cabinet.
Hrmm, you appear to be a little overburdened. Shed yourself some of thy worldly trappings and then come speak to me again.
Unleash the curse!
Step away from the door.
Another dragon down, eh? The mainland must be missing you! I bet you'd have solved half the world's problems by now.

Hey there friend, good to see you again. The Wise Old Man was getting on my nerves a bit, so I thought I might try and give you a hand. Been looking into everything and you're not gonna want to hear this, but there's another ruddy dragon at play. Only, get this, she's already dead.
As for me, nothing new really. Death's not come to reap me yet, think he might even like me. Maybe if I keep working along side you I can stave off the ever-after for a little while longer.

There are some lingering ghostly echoes around the place, and I got talking to them. Seems like there was this big friendly dragon called Imaru, who turned somewhat unfriendly after being killed by some other, bigger, less-friendly dragon. Now she's stuck in the afterlife, eating any unfortunate souls that come her way.

So, you think those stones mean something? Feels like they're pointing to something important. There's a lot of necromantic magic whizzing around here, and these things seem to be the focus of it all.
There's something strange about these stones, they're a focus point for a whole load of necromantic energy. Maybe try reading them?
I've spotted this great keep up on the mountains. Feels like there might be someone alive there. What do you say? Meet you there? One last great adventure or something like that?
All these shambling corpses causing trouble, that's her doing. Their spirits ripped out of them, leaving just enough to keep them wandering.
If I wasn't a misty cloud of regret in a vaguely human shape, I'd try and work out what those stones are pointing to, and then deal with whatever's there.

Pieces of Imaru's curse, just up for grabs? Feels like someone's laid a trap for big, mean and scaly. I'll leave it to you to go and collect them, I don't think I'm going to do much against a dragon that eats wandering souls.

Great work on that first seal! You're already looking stronger, spiritually speaking. Get the other two and we should be able to deal with Imaru. By we, I mean you, obviously, but I'll be cheering from the sides... very far away sides.
Two down, one to go. You've really got the hang of this adventurer gig. I'm kinda jealous, I'd always wanted to be one of the heroic types. Great adventures, derring-dos and all that.

Now, normally I'd say you should go and give her hell, but get this - she's not just a dragon, she's a CURSED dragon! And this curse, it makes her bigger, nastier and generally unstoppable. Someone did some proper dark magic here to get that going, but if you're going to take this dragon out, you need to deal with that somehow.
Being sacrificed to a dragon somewhat ruins that. Still, I'm going to try my best at the ghostly sidekick gig. Maybe I can be a footnote in one of your adventures somewhere?
That's all of the seals. Wow, you're really good at this. I thought I was cut out to be an adventurer, but compared to you I'm a joke.
Dragons don't stand a chance against you! Best go speak to big tall and boney, so he can confirm she's dead and gone. I'll wait here, I guess.

I'm not exactly knowledgeable about curses, but I can feel a strange sort of necromantic power in the air. It mostly focuses over the big tower over there, like a ward keeping us out, but it also converges here by these stones. Something odd about them. Worth a look?
Ha! Wish I'd learned that before I died, it would have made things a whole lot easier, and I'd probably still be alive today. Still, no point dwelling over spilled arterial fluid.

Now that you've got yourself nice and cursed, you can breach the tower right? Time to take on Imaru and destroy her once and for all! I wish I could join you, but I'll be there in spirit. Well... not literally, cos she eats those, but you know what I mean.

Now, before you go anywhere, there's something I'd like to discuss. Soul fragments. These little stones are of no use to you, but very useful to me. They contain the last traces of the poor lost souls of Fellhollow, and I would like to help them move on.

If you come across any of these soul fragments, please bring them to me and I will happily exchange them for special items you cannot get anywhere else. Here, let me show you some of the items available to you.
Now then, what do you need?
What would you like to know?
Ah, but you know me already, don't you? I am the shadow over your shoulder, inching ever closer until you take that final breath. You have always known me, because you await me each day.
The waters of the River Noumenon flow into this region, and to be clear they shouldn't. Something about this place has caused damage enough to the Underworld to harm the world of the living as well.
Imagine, for a moment, that your soul is on a string and that string gets snagged round a tree. As your body walks, the essence that is you gets pulled further and further away.

There is a life after death, that's one great mystery answered for you - you're welcome. When a person dies I cut the cord connecting their soul to their body and allow them to pass into the Underworld.
Or, you can call me Harold, though few ever do. I was once like you, just a normal man, living a normal life -- a farmer, I think, though it's difficult to remember so long ago.
Whatever is happening prevents souls from reaching the Afterlife. More than that, it seems to prevent my ability to reap them. They are all off my list, and that's just not proper.
You start to see the world as a spirit would. As everything around you drains of life, colour and vibrancy, you see the hidden things that lie beneath the glamour of living.
In the Underworld, a great river, the river Noumenon, carries souls down to mighty gates that lead to what lies beyond. What happens next is a mystery, even to me.

I died, that's what got me this job. I was the very first person to die on Gielinor. Hardly the most glamorous of accolades, but someone had to. In so dying I became Death, capital D, the reaper of souls.

This isn't just people either. Animals, even the plants, have had some of their vitality drawn out of them. Even the water is tainted with the essence of the river Noumenon -- meaning you need to be careful trying to drink it.

Yet, with each step, you lose more and more of that grasp on life. Your soul is tugged further and further from your body until finally... SNAP! Your tether breaks and your soul is lost to the twilight.
The Menaphite god Icthlarin, guards souls as they pass through the gate. Time was that Amascut would offer some souls rebirth, but things have been... tricky, on that front for a while.
Guthix himself gave me the scythe and robes I use to this day. It is my honour and my duty to cut the tether that traps souls to this world, allowing the dead to move on to the Underworld.
The land is cursed and dangerous. The perfect place for an adventurer like yourself to cut their teeth, no?
Yet, it is not your time and you did not pass naturally. Your body, while dead, still wanders because it is now driven not by your will, but by instinct, hunger and a need to live again.
But, death isn't really something you need to worry about for a while. I've decided to keep you from passing on until you've cleared up a few problems for me. Just don't get too carried away.

It's a lonely old job, sometimes, and the paperwork will drive you to madness. But, I have Muncher to help with the lonliness, and all the time in the world to make a decent headstart on the paperwork.

That is the curse that afflicts Fellhollow. Raising the dead as mindless creatures, and forcing the souls to wander the world unable to pass on. Doomed to lose themselves and go mad from the lonely horror of it all.

Still, when Gielinor itself dies and I can retire, I suspect there will still be more forms to fill in than there are stars in the skies. Only two things in life are guaranteed, death and paperwork... and the former is debatable.
In short, it's a bad thing. Probably want to deal with it quickly.
Ask about the Underworld
Ask about Death.
Ask about Fellhollow
Ask about Wither Rot

[Exchange Soul Fragments]
Strange magic radiates off the door. It seems like it requires a phrase of some kind to access.
Strange magic radiates off the door. It seems like it requires a phrase of some kind to access.
Nothing interesting happens.
Nothing interesting happens.
Knock knock!
Open sesame!
Oi! Let me in!
Open sesame!
Mors, introitum quaero!
Knock knock!
Oi! Let me in!
How can I help?
How can I help?
Oh, ho, ho. Getting waay a-head of yourself here. I think you should go speak to tall, dark and spooky back there, huh?
Oh dear, look at you running a-head of yourself. You're all soul rifted, and that's gonna get painful quick. You should go speak to Death before you do yourself a mischief.
Oh, ho, ho. Getting waay a-head of yourself here. I think you should go speak to tall, dark and spooky back there, huh?
Enjoying yourself in Fellhollow? Yeah, I wouldn't take a holiday there either. Don't do too many holidays anyway, I don't like spending them on my own and, well, I've just got no-body to go with.
Oh dear, looking a bit peaky there. You should find yourself a rejuvination pool before Imaru spots you. Trust me.
Yeah, Fellhollow's a bit of a nightmare, isn't it? You're absolutely doomed mate. Haha, just ribbing you! I'm sure you've got this all under control.

Nice work in Fellhollow! You're really a step a-head of the mainland adventurers. Now that things have calmed down a bit, I've got decades worth of letters to deliver. So I'm just gonna rest here a bit before I start.

Hey there, bit lost? No-body to point you in the right direction for a good tailor?... Because, frankly, your look could use some work. I assume you're trying to get into Fellhollow? Nasty place. I wouldn't be seen dead there.
Ah, feel a little light in the soul there? That's Soul Rift for you. On the plus side, you'll see things you couldn't see before. On the downside you're a dragon's dinner waiting to happen.

Nice work in Fellhollow! You're really a step a-head of the mainland adventurers. Now that things have calmed down a bit, I've got decades worth of letters to deliver. So I'm just gonna rest here a bit before I start.

Still, if you're determined to head on through, you'll need to shed a few pounds. You need to get Soulrifted, my friend. Need to get that spirit of yours dragged a little into the world of the dead. It's the only way to get through this here gate.
You don't want to stay soul rifted for too long. As time goes on you'll attract the hungry dead to you, eventually luring Imaru herself and... well... that won't end well for you.

See that horrible red stuff over there? I know it looks nasty, I certainly wouldn't have the stomach for it, but you're going to need to dip your toes in for a minute or two to get nice and Soulrifted. That'll let you see things you living types never get to see.
So, if I were you -- and I had feet -- I'd get my skates on and make a beeline straight for a purification pool. You can't miss them, Death's made them extra glowy, just for you!

You'll want to find a Purification Pool, once you've found your way past that wall. There's one down the path outta here, I think, but I'm getting a-head of myself there. Get to it quick, the longer you're soul rifted, the more likely *she* is to spot you, and the worse things will get. If that dragon finds you, you're dead, no two ways about it.
Oh! When you've done all of that, come back and see me, I've got something I could use a hand with. An actual hand, since I don't have them.
