The shrine hums with magical power, weakening the barrier enchantment around Emberwood village.
You repair the broken shrine. Magic thrums into life, feeding energy back to the village barrier.
The shrine is damaged, a piece missing. Until it is repaired the magic cannot flow to the village barrier.
Saradomin shields this village from the relentless dead. Seek his power on high, surrounded by a ring of water. Obtain the blessings of all the gods to destroy the barrier.
The statue no longer maintains the barrier to the village.
The power of chaos wards this village form harm. Hail Zamorak! Seek his altar near by, where the suffering is strongest. Obtain the blessings of all the gods to destroy the barrier.
The statue no longer maintains the barrier to the village.
The lord of balance leaves his blessing in a harmonious circle, guarded by a dread beast. Obtain the blessings of all the gods to destroy the barrier.
The statue no longer maintains the barrier to the village.

Justice must be maintained, even in times of great strife. Seek the wisdom of Armadyl on a nearby lake, where three spirits await judgement.  Obtain the blessings of all the gods to destroy the barrier.
The statue no longer maintains the barrier to the village.
You offer a prayer to the shrine and it hums with magical energy. The barrier around the village weakens.
The shrine hums with magical power, weakening the barrier around Emberwood Village.
You offer a prayer to the shrine, and it hums with magical power. The barrier around Emberwood village weakens as a result.
The shrine hums with magical power, weakening the barrier around Emberwood Village.

Justice must prevail, for the barrier to rise. Such is the will of Armadyl. Long ago a terrible act was committed. What was the crime? Who is responsible and why did they do it? Name these and unlock the blessing of Armadyl.
Cast your verdict arbiter. What crime was committed?
The shrine hums with magical power, weakening the barrier.

I shouldn't be here. I deserve to move on! I was there, sure, when the bodies piled up, but I had nothing to do with it. It was a sunny day, the light was in my eyes and there were rabbits everywhere and I just thought, why not? You know? There's good eating on one of those.

I never get invited to parties, but this house party was something special, you know? A great achievement, deserving of celebration, how could I turn it down? We laughed, we drank, we danced the night away, it was wonderful. Partying till morning, in the glare of the sun.
It was a lovely house party, really it was. But, the weather was cold and grey, and I just wanted to go for a walk, you know? So that's why I was there, in the park, when  the trouble started.
Nothing else here but rubble.
You have no room in your inventory to pick up the statue piece.
The dragon's power prevents you from using this.
Speak to the ghosts to learn their take on the events. Look for the discrepancies and the emotions at play, the guilty often trap themselves with their own lies.
We thought we might end celebrations at the Party Room, you know? Balloons, prizes, everyone having the time of their lives? Sure, we were a bit drunk, but who wouldn't be after an all night rager?

I'd just been wandering over by the party room, the sound of balloons popping is soothing, you know? I had my bow out, because, well, I thought I could shoot a couple of them that floated away. Balloons, obviously.
You collect the broken statue piece.
Incorrect. An arbiter must not be so blind to the crimes committed. Speak to the spirits again to learn the true crime committed.
Indeed, a brutal and terrible crime. Many lives lost in an instant, their families deprived of their loved ones. Tell me, why was such an act committed?

So, I took a shot, even though the glare made it hard to see and, well, next thing I know there's screaming. I ran, I admit it. I ran from the city gate, all the way to the party room. I figured music and revelry would keep me safe, right?
I think it was the laughing that came first. Loud and obnoxious, a guffawing cackle that we heard over the screaming. They thought it was funny, as they tore the city apart. Laughing as they went.
Ha! Then the screaming happened, man it was funny!

When the balloons started popping, I just assumed it was another drop party, you know? I figured there was always a chance I could get something from one, like a party hat or something. But they weren't popping because of parties, they were popping because the arrows went flying.
Incorrect. An arbiter must not be so blind to the crimes committed. Speak to the spirits again to learn the true crime committed.

Yes. Imagine, an act of such violence, such tragedy and loss. Families ruined. Destinies upended. Futures shattered. All because someone found it amusing. As though the lives of others carry no more weight than an ant beneath ones boot. But, tell me, who committed the crime?
So many dead. Falador lined with bodies. But, it wasn't me, honest. I had nothing to do with it. I was just hunting rabbits.

What? Oh, come on, you'd have been laughing too. Balloons exploding as people fell over them running, you can't not laugh at that? It was all "Aaargh *POP* Noooo! *POP* My precious spleen!" how is that not funny?
What makes you suspect them?
What makes you suspect them?
What makes you suspect them?
Sure, in the chaos, I stole a couple of gemstones someone left as they ran. But, i mean, come on, it was a drop party after all! Fair game. I shouldn't have to suffer because of that.
An interesting deduction, but an incorrect one. Speak to the spirits once more and look for the discrepancies in their tales.
Yes, the guilty often miss the smaller details as they try to pretend their innocence. This spirit was responsible for the destruction and will pay the price in the afterlife.

Yes. Sometimes the guilty lack shame, or remorse, unable to keep their strange sense of pride hidden. To them, this massacre was an amusement, a bit of a laugh. To others, it was the worst day of their lives... or their last.
The shrine hums with magical power, weakening the barrier.
They lied about the weather.
To complete a demonic ritual.
Because they thought it was funny.
A noble was assassinated.
To spread fear among the population.
There was a mass murder.
A bank was robbed.
It was all about money.
The Suspicious Ghost.
The Snickering Ghost.
They found it too funny. Matching the motive.
The Shady Ghost.
Just because.
They have a very annoying laugh.
They admitted to being armed.
They're very shady.
There are no rabbits in Falador.
Just because.
They admitted to stealing gemstones.
They're very suspicious.
They were drunk, but their story was too detailed.
Just because.
A magical artifact was stolen.

Quest_DogDays.description: Investigate the Garou and their rituals.

objectives.text: Search Garou camps beneath giant wyrm bones in the Highlands for information on Garou ritual practices.
Challenge a Garou king in their Highland stronghold and claim their token.
Search garou camps beneath the giant wyrm bones in the Highlands for information on the King's Token.
Complete the ritual of purification on the King's Token at the ancient shrine where "a heart once beat".
Bring the Purified King's Token to Vannaka in the Ghornfell Highlands.
Search the Ghornfell Highlands for a friendly face with an interest in Garou rituals.

dialogueRefs.text: It is strange how a simple trinket can give you such a strong sense of connection. It feels like a piece of me pining for home.
The animal within me, remembering a part of itself. And, for the first time in as long as I can remember, the beast does not stir.
The animal within me, remembering a part of itself. And, for the first time in as long as I can remember, the beast does not stir.
You've come a long way, young pup, good to see. I'm here studying a race not seen for hundreds of years - the Garou.
This shrine appears to be part of a garou ritual of some kind.
I have run from my wolf my entire life. Feared its fangs and claws. But, now, perhaps I can allow myself to face it.
Ah, yes, sorry, this won't mean anything to you. Pay an old fool no mind.
Found anything interesting yet, young pup? No? Pity. Perhaps take a look through some of the garou camps?
Found anything interesting yet, young pup? Hrmm, you took a token from a garou king?
Found anything interesting yet, young pup? Hrmm, some writing on a ritual? Let me take a look...
Found anything interesting yet, young pup? Oh? You have the king's token? Let me see...
Ah, there it is. May I see it? The purified token?
You've come a long way, young pup, good to see. I'm here studying a race not seen for hundreds of years - the Garou.
I came here to uncover the truth. I heard tale of a ritual to preserve a fragment of a legacy my family has forgotten.
This shrine is dedicated to Lougrim, and looks like the place referred to in the Ritual of Purification. You have everything you need to perform the ritual.
They make their homes in the spines of the dead wyrms around here, why not give them a look?.
I'm impressed, that's no easy feat, that. Defeating a garou king.
This... this is what I'm looking for. A ritual to take a piece of Antumnos, the primordial forest.
It's not quite right. It feels tainted, as if it's forgotten where it's from. Wait... that ritual you found, that's the answer!
This... this trinket may seem like nothing to you. But for me it's an anchor to my ancestral home...
What? You've uncovered a ritual text? Let me take a look at that.
Wait... that token. You've slain their king? May I see the token? Yes, yes, I thought so. This is almost what I'm looking for. Almost.
Wait... that token. May I see it? The purified token?
I've been scouring garou camps, but I need your help and, well, a burden shared is a burden halved, eh?
This shrine is dedicated to Lougrim, and looks like the place referred to in the Ritual of Purification. If you had the King's Token, 2 ram horns and 3 shock bulbs, you could perform the ritual here.
They make their homes in the spines of the dead wyrms around here, why not give them a look?.
But this... is almost what I'm looking for. A piece of Antumnos, though it seems... sullied, somehow.
A ritual of purification, to turn this sullied trinket into a true piece of the Antumnos, the ancestral home.
This... this is what I've been looking for. A chance to own a piece of the Ancestral world.
This is a piece of the ancestral world of the garou, but it's been corrupted by this world and needs purification.
They tend to camp beneath the spines of great wyrm remains. Scout those bones and let me know if you uncover anything.

For a fraction of a moment the shrine is bathed in ethereal moonlight that shines from the ritual writing engraved on its surface. The King's Token seems different somehow, cleaner, lighter and somehow whole.
It's a personal matter. An old family interest, shall we say?
They may seem brutal and savage, the garou, and frankly they are -- But there's a deeper spirituality to them as well.
Few places embody "survival of the fittest" quite like here.
Where, might be better. It is the primordial forest, a world far far from ours.
I... this is important to me, young pup. I ask that you keep looking. See if you can complete this ritual and bring me the token.
I... I need you to do this for me, young pup. Complete that ritual and purify the token. I'll explain everything on your return.
Aye, yes. an explanation. See, the garou weren't always on Ashenfall. They came from far, far away.
Hrmm, looks like you're carrying too much, young pup. Best lighten your load before I can give you this.
Young pup, please, you must complete this ritual for me. I... I cannot say why, just yet, but it is important to me.
I came here to uncover the truth. I heard tale of a ritual to preserve a fragment of a legacy my family has forgotten.
My family has a history with the beastmen, dating back over the ages.
I know, I know. What does a slayer master care about spirituality? But that's exactly the point, you see...
The garou, the wildlife, even the very weather wants you dead. This place makes you face your mortality, lets you know you're alive.
One in which the wild grows free and unhindered by the yoke of so called "civilisation".
I need you to look around, see if there's anything you can do to purify it. To make it a pure piece of that long lost place.
I'll explain everything once you do. .
I... I need you to do this for me, young pup. Complete that ritual and purify the token. I'll explain everything on your return.
Sometime in the third age, I think, they were captured by Zamorakian forces and there they became part of a vampyre experiment, to create something new.
Your journey begins with the death of the garou king. Go! Paint the earth with his blood. History favours the bold, and the bold carve their legend into the bones of the fallen.
Could you look into this? Check the garou camps, beneath the spines of great wyrm remains. Let me know if you uncover anything.
Like we slayer masters, the garou are primal creatures. We understand the need to be hunter, not prey.
The whole place is littered with the bones of great wyrms. Beasts so terrible I'm glad they're dead.
It has always been of interest to me, ever since my mother told me legends of such a place when I was a child.
I need you to look around, see if there's anything you can do to purify it. To make it a pure piece of that long lost place.
I'll explain everything once you do. .
My family has a history with the beastmen, dating back over the ages.
The garou honour that truth, in every part of their culture. I find it... comforting.
Even I would think twice about trying to hunt one of those down. But here, the garou make their bones their home.
I believe the garou lived there once, before their goddess took them here.
No, you're right, I'm sorry to trouble you. Here, something to thank you for your effort.
My ancesters... the werewolves. Aye, yes, my biggest secret. Tooth and claw beneath the silvery moon.
There's something beautiful about that, in a weird sort of way. Sheltering the shadow of monsters slain.
I left my people to try and hide from the beast, but it's always followed me... and been used against me.
The garou honour that truth, in every part of their culture. I find it... comforting.
I believe the garou lived there once, before their goddess took them here.
I don't want to hide any more. And this trinket will be a link to my ancestors, something to help me make peace with the beast.
There's something beautiful about that, in a weird sort of way. Sheltering the shadow of monsters slain.
Here, something to show my gratitude for this piece of family history.
Perform the Ritual of Purification
What can you tell me about the Garou?
Why are you interested in garou rituals?
Don't perform the Ritual of Purification
What can you tell me about the Highlands?
I don't need an explanation.
What do you mean?
What's Antumnos?
Test
Night 1
Day 1
Day 2
Night 2
What now
Ok bye
Tell me more
That's enough.

Quest_DragonSlayer.description: Recruited with promises of glory, your first challenge is to defeat General Velgar.

objectives.text: Construct a base of operations in Bramblemead village. Build a shelter and claim a bed.

objectives.id: Return to the Wise old man after claimed bed
objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man in Bramblemead village.
Hunt a deer and bring one of its antlers to the Wise Old Man.
Siege the goblin castle and look for Cathan.
Investigate the blue-flame door in the swamp. Find out what Cathan is up to.

objectives.id: Return to the Wise old man
objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man in Bramblemead village.
Gear yourself up and push forward into Ghornfell in search of Cathan.

objectives.id: Look for evidence of Cathan at the tower
objectives.text: Investigate Velgar's tower in search of Cathan.
Find the ingredients and craft the Challenge Horn. Check the recipe in your journal for more information.
Summon and defeat Velgar.

objectives.id: Return to the Wise old man after killing velgar
objectives.text: Bring Velgar's head to the Wise Old Man outside Velgar's Lair.

details.textName: Return to the Wise old man after claimed bed
Return to the Wise old man
Look for evidence of Cathan at the tower
Return to the Wise old man after killing velgar

dialogueRefs.text: Good, you've got the basics under your belt, but now the guide ropes are off. Taking down a dragon won't be easy, but you've got the skills you need to do it. Well... almost.
We need to start thinking long term. Bramblemead village is an excellent place for an outpost, even if it's a little overrun with goblins right now.
Not finished yet? The longer you leave things, the more likely you are to become a dragon's dinner.
Good, you've built a shelter. I mean... it could do with some work, we're gonna be here a while. Have you considered the decor at all?
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
Maybe some better lighting? Curtains? A single potted plant? *Sigh* no, no, you're right. It's not important. Why live it up when there's so much squalor to enjoy?
Doesn't need to be fancy -- though style is always worth pursuing -- but it needs to be functional. Make a shelter, some foundations, walls, and a roof, and then build and claim a bed in it.
Doesn't need to be fancy -- though style is always worth pursuing -- but it needs to be functional. Make a shelter, some foundations, walls, and a roof, and then build and claim a bed in it.
Anyway, look, we're set up here, but there's one of our number missing. Young Cathan, an adventurer in training that came along with us.
You can go bigger, of course, let your inner architect run wild, but the bed's the bare minimum we need to get started. Go on, hop to it. Get!
You can go bigger, of course, let your inner architect run wild, but the bed's the bare minimum we need to get started. Go on, hop to it. Get!
He disappeared after we got the lodestone working, vanished before you arrived. I'd like to track him down. To do that I need to cast a locator spell.
I'm just missing one ingredient, which I'll need from you. Antlers. You can get them from deer, hunt one and bring me the antlers. Then we'll get started. But first, here, take this.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
Ah... the castle, not ideal. That place is a veritable goblin stronghold. Go see if you can find him, but make sure you're geared up for a fight.
Argh, leave me alone human.
I still ain't talkin' to no stinky human. Get lost!
So, young Cathan's pushing his way into Ghornfell, eh? Reckless, as always, that boy's gonna get himself killed.
Any sign of young Cathan? What -- he escaped, even managed to turn a few goblins to his cause? Interesting lad that, going to go places.
Oh no, not another human. You gonna just leave me to die too? Like the last one did?
Not found young Cathan yet? Last we heard he'd been captured by the goblins up at the Brynmoor Castle. I'll need you to storm in there and rescue him.
Hrmm? How are you getting on? Got me any antlers yet?
But, if he's braving the garou, he must know a way of dealing with Velgar. There's no other reason he'd do something quite so stupid.
Speaking of going places, you mention he's exploring a dragonkin vault in the swamps? I think you probably want to go and take a look. No?
Got us all riled up. Promised us power and glory. Said he knews how to get rid of the big scaly war king.
Look, I hate to ask this, but I need you to go after him. You need to fight your way into Ghornfell and pick up his trail.
Well he got what he wanted, some weird dragonkin stuff, then he said he were heading into Ghornfell and that I'd just slow us down. The others agreed, gits.
Ah excellent, you've got one, we can begin. This ritual is a bit old school, proper druidic guff, but it's handy in a pinch.
Not got the ingredients yet? I need you to hunt a deer and bring me one of their antlers. Deers are flighty creatures, and easily spooked.
You're really struggling with this, aren't you? I'll walk you through exactly what to do, but I can't be holding your hand all the time.
Ghornfell's no joke though, that's where the garou live and if you thought goblins were trouble you're in for a shock.
So I bet you're just like him, so I aint gonna talk to yous no more. Yeah, that'll teach yas!
It homes in on the spiritual residue of our subject, in this case young Cathan, using this old shoe of his as a spiritual connection. Vile, but useful. Just don't sniff it.
Discover, learn and improve. That's going to need to be your mantra on Ashenfall if you're going to survive. So find new materials, discover new recipes and then make them.
Horrible creatures, the garou. Deadly beastmen with no concept of mercy. You'll need to make sure you're as prepared as you can be, before you risk facing them in battle.
We'll then just point the antler at the map, and it'll point straight to where we'll find him... or at least where he's been most the last couple of days.
You'll find it easier to hunt one if you craft yourself a bow of some kind. The deer themselves are all over Bramblemead, finding them shouldn't be a problem.
To hunt deer you'll want a bow. Find some flax and some wood, this should be enough to help you build a spinning wheel. There you'll make thread and with that you can craft a bow.
Here, this'll help get you started.
Now then, we just need to spread the rune essence like so. Add a dash of this weird unguent stuff Zanik made from snails, and then...
Just hunt one down, and bring me the antlers. You can keep all the other useful materials, maybe use them to craft better gear? You're looking a bit shabby.
Find feathers to make arrows, and then you're good to go. While you're at it, look for recipes that will let you make stronger gear. You're going to need it.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
I need you to gear yourself up as best you can, then push into Ghornfel to look for young Cathan.
Oh dear... I'm dead...
Make the horn, summon the dragon and then kick his ass for me. I'm counting on you, hero, we all are.
Ghornfell is a dangerous place, and home to the garou beastmen. Keep your wits about you.
You've made it into Ghornfel, I'm impressed. No, honestly, I expected you to drown in the swamp or something.
Cathan's dead? To shreds you say? Poor lad, not the end he deserved. But Velgar's made a mistake here, he's made this personal.
So, first off, death sucks. Let's just get that out of the way. I figured I might at least stand a chance against Velgar, I had all the plans, and I am sure I could have beaten him.
You did it! Velgar got what he deserved. Thank you, hero, now I can rest in peace.
But if the entrance to Ghornfel is what you say, it sounds like Cathan has been captured...again... so I need you to go and rescue him.
I generally discourage violence, but this time I think you need to gather as much of it as possible and serve up a dragon sized portion.
But then his garou minions mobbed me and dragged me here. They held me down as Velgar watched, laughing as they sacrificed me!
Make the horn, summon the dragon and then kick his ass for me. I'm counting on you, hero, we all are.
I imagine the garou will be taking him to Velgar. Make your way to the tower, and pray you're not too late.
Build the horn. Summon Velgar. Avenge Cathan, save us all. Punch a dragon in the face!
As death's go it could have been more heroic. Not exactly what I wanted on my epitaph. But, hey, silver cloud, you can avenge me now!
Here, let me teach you a recipe. It's a dragonkin horn that will force Velgar to battle. It's got to be used here, in an altar on the tower, but Velgar can't refuse it.
Make the horn, summon the dragon and then kick his ass for me. I'm counting on you, hero, we all are.
Cathan's dead? To shreds you say? Poor lad, not the end he deserved. But Velgar's made a mistake here, he's made this personal.
I generally discourage violence, but this time I think you need to gather as much of it as possible and serve up a dragon sized portion.
Build the horn. Summon Velgar. Avenge Cathan, save us all. Punch a dragon in the face!
Cathan's dead? To shreds you say? Poor lad, not the end he deserved. But Velgar's made a mistake here, he's made this personal.
There is an indention in the altar where something would be placed. It looks like it would fit the shape of Cathan's summoning horn design.
What's that? Velgar's dead? Are you sure? I'll need to see his head, dragons can be tricky like that.
The dragon's dead, that's quite the victory. No, really, you should be proud of yourself!
I generally discourage violence, but this time I think you need to gather as much of it as possible and serve up a dragon sized portion.
There is an indention in the altar where something would be placed. It looks like it would fit the shape of Cathan's summoning horn design.
There is an indentation in the altar where something would be placed, but you are not sure what it might be.
Bring me his head and I'll make sure you're rewarded.
It's not every day you take out a draconic general infused with the elemental power of the earth. But you managed it, well done!
Build the horn. Summon Velgar. Avenge Cathan, save us all. Punch a dragon in the face!
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.

Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know. There's a strange door to the north, just past Ashien's Watch and it's sending chills down my spine. Meet me there, we'll talk more.
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Place the horn and summon Velgar>
<Step away from the altar>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>
Anything else I can help you with?
When my comrades and I set foot on Ashenfall, we thought it would be paradise. Lush green fields, tall and resilient trees – a world unsullied.
General Velgar, let that sink in. A title, on a dragon, not a good sign.
I know very little about this Kuldra character, except that Velgar pledged his loyalty to her.
Cathan, now there was a pain in the neck.
Relatively little is known about the Dragonkin, less still the ones who set up shop here.
I don't have much for you there, Vannaka's the one investigating them. He's pushing his way into Ghornfell, you should look for him there.
But then dragons happened.
We don't know much at the moment, since everyone who's seen him is dead.
From what I can gather, she's something like royalty to the dragons here; never a good sign.
Young noble sprog, low down the pecking order. Fifth son, I think. Wanted to be a hero, you know how it goes.
We know that they're ancient, dangerous and constantly angry. They were cursed by the elder gods a long, long, long time ago.
What I know is that the garou are merciless. They'll cut you down without a chance to speak.
They swooped down from the skies and decimated the landing party. Whole teams of people, gone, just like that.
But he's big, scary and he wants to make all of us wyrm food. So, diplomacy's out.
She's spoken of not with the reverence due a monarch, but with the devotion due a deity.
Got into scraps as a boy. Lost his leg to a wolf. Say what you want, he had guts that kid.
They have a penchant for two things that interest us. First, they make dragons, which is the problem we're facing right now.
Beastmen from another world, living only for the hunt. Best avoided if you can, but be prepared for a tough fight where you can't.
"Queen Kuldra bids you welcome," they laughed, as our comrades drew their final breaths.
I don't like that. Not one itty little bit.
The "legendary" swordsman Vannaka taught him the art of swordplay, while I instructed him in the arcane.
Secondly, they hoard secrets like they're more valuable than gold... or party hats.
He was a constant annoyance—loud, irritating, overflowing with relentless optimism. You know the type. Even so, his absence leaves a void.
Their vaults will be guarded, but well worth exploring. You never know what you might find in there.
So here's the deal: I need you to kill them all. Show these dragons and their Queen, that we're not just going to roll over and die.
We fight back, and we fight back hard.
Tell me more about these dragons.
Can you tell me about the Dragonkin?
Can you tell me about the Garou?
Can you tell me about Queen Kuldra?
Can you tell me about the previous adventurer?
Can you tell me about Velgar?
Oh, cease your cowering, you're not dead. You still have at least twenty minutes before I reap your soul.

I need you to investigate Fellhollow. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

Haha, just a little joke... Mostly. You'll probably die a few times, but I'll bring you back like I have been doing. I still have work for you after all. I know why you're here, little bit of a problem with the dead not actually dying.

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.

Thought I'd do some exploring, it gets boring sitting in a ruined little village all the time... so I found a new ruined area, but this time with angry dog-people. Anyway, they leave me alone, I leave them alone.

Welcome to Fellhollow. The whole region is infected with a terrible withering. Some dread curse that untethers the soul and drags it to the river Noumenon without ever sailing upon it, preventing the dead from moving on. This cannot stand.
I don't know what you're talking to me for. Aren't you busy doing stuff through that creepy door down this tunnel? Go on, get!
Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know.
The thing that really interests me though is down this little passageway. There's a door, and it's sealed by magic. Strange stuff too, old and powerful. It'll take me some time to work it out.

I need you to investigate this. Find out what went on. Resolve it if you can and I shall reward you for your efforts. As well as continue this little resurrection situation. A fair bargain, I'm sure you agree.

See this creepy little passageway? There's a door at the bottom wreathed in magic, and the spooky stuff at that -- necromancy. I've been studying it for a while and I've learned the words to allow access.
But, anyway, aren't you busy? Shouldn't you be off looking at how best to stab old Velgar to death? Feels like you should be focusing your attention on that, hrmm? Go on, get!
The dragon's dead, that's quite the victory. No, really, you should be proud of yourself!

I would start by seeking out an old friend of yours, young Cathan. He's been doing some work for me, investigating the site of some necromantic ritual or other. Before you do that, though, you'll need to get into Fellhollow. A colleague of mine, Postie Pete, can help you with that.
Obviously, I'm not going to open it, so I'm giving the words to you. You need to go up to the door and say "Mors, introitum quaero!" and it should let you in.
It's not every day you take out a draconic general infused with the elemental power of the earth. But you managed it, well done!
Well? Go on, get! I don't have all day to hold your hand. There's something weird and sinister, go poke it with a stick like you always do!
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>

Quest_ElderGarou.description: An elder garou wants you to build a home that his late wife would be proud of.

objectives.text: Build a home around Caratacus the Elder.

dialogueRefs.text: Ah…footsteps.
The home you once built me is now gone.
I feel my wife's hand on my shoulder. I thought it was Death's at first, but it's not. It's her.
I can feel it; solace from the wind. The house…it stands now, doesn’t it?
I can sense her happiness. Her calm. I cannot thank you enough, traveller.
You’ve done an old garou a great kindness. Thank you, traveller.
A traveller, I think.
Tell me…does the house stand yet on the cliffs?
Do you need something, traveller?
My wife chose this beautiful spot on the cliffs overlooking the sea. She said it would be the perfect place for a little wooden home.
An old garou cannot build it alone. When the walls rise and the roof covers me, come speak to me.
I remember when I first saw her. Someone had been stealing from our tribe. Taking meat and pelts.
You’ve done an old garou a great kindness. Thank you, traveller.
I always meant to build it for her, but time has made these old bones slow, and these eyes see nothing now.
I was posted as guard. She was so noisy, I was surprised that no one had heard her steal from us before.
It’s a beautiful place. I can hear the waves from here.
Her eyes locked onto mine, but she didn't stop or run away. She continued to load herself with spoils while staring at me.
Would you help an old garou to build a home that my wife would be proud of? Be sure it covers me.
She kept that look until her last days. I saw it whenever she snatched food from my plate. And that was often.
Ah, Cliodhna. I still serve myself too much food. Always for you.
Nothing, thanks
Could you tell me more about her?

Quest_FH_CollectorsCalling.description: Doric is looking for rare weapons in Fellhollow.

objectives.text: Craft an Undead Ranger's Bow and bring it to Doric in Fellhollow. Doric believes the recipe is in a vault somewhere.
Craft a Shadow Sword and bring it to Doric in Fellhollow. Doric believes a zogre has the recipe.
Craft a Necromancer's Staff and bring it to Doric in Fellhollow. Doric believes the recipe is in a vault somewhere.
Speak to Doric in Fellhollow.

dialogueRefs.text: Thanks for all your help. Ashenfall really is home to some remarkable weapons. I wonder what else we'll uncover? My boy, Boric, would love this place.
You know what, we make a good team, you and I. You find me things and I record them for future crafters to enjoy.
It may not sound like much, but sharing knowledge is what turns a gathering of people into a thriving community.
You know what, we make a good team, you and I. You find me things and I record them for future crafters to enjoy.
Amazing, you've got the staff! That's... that's exactly like the story... this is... hrmm. Why would this story be so accurate, unless...
I'm looking for a necromancer's staff. Perhaps it's another weapon in one of those dragonkin vaults?
Well now, there you have it! A shadow sword!
We're looking for a shadow sword. When I was investigating the area the clues I found pointed to one of those zogre things. You might need to kill quite a few of them.
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
I'm looking for an undead ranger's bow. Perhaps it's another weapon in one of those dragonkin vaults?
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
That's it! That's the bow! It looks just like the story described. I wonder...
It's all like the story. You know, I used to tell my boy this story, good old Boric. He was so excited to hear the tale of heroic warriors and undead monsters.
Ah, yes, you must be quite busy. Well, I won't keep you. If you're bored later, come say hi.
Wonderful. Now then, I once told me lad about this strange warrior from far away. Fought great evil, undead beasties and the like.
Wonderful. Now then, I once told me lad about this strange warrior from far away. Fought great evil, undead beasties and the like.
Ah, yes, you must be quite busy. Well, I won't keep you. If you're bored later, come say hi.
Here, my little way of saying thank you.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
To think, I'm standing in the very land this story took place. Boric would love to hear this... if... if I ever get a chance to see him again of course.
Sounds familiar, doesn't it? A land full of the undead, with deadly monsters roaming around. I'm now wondering if the story came from here somehow.
Sounds familiar, doesn't it? A land full of the undead, with deadly monsters roaming around. I'm now wondering if the story came from here somehow.
Here, a little something for your troubles.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
Ah don't mind me. Just a melancholic old man worried about his fully grown and perfectly capable boy. I just don't tell him enough how proud of him I am.
As the tale goes, the warrior first had to face off against a deadly archer. All bone and dark magic. Had this skeletal bow that was described in eerie detail.
As the tale goes, the warrior first had to face off against a deadly archer. All bone and dark magic. Had this skeletal bow that was described in eerie detail.
OK, let's look at the next part of the story. There was a necromancer, nasty piece of work, with a powerful magic staff.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
Anyway, here, have this. My little way of saying thank you for helping an old codger like me connect to happy memories.
If you can find and make me that undead ranger's bow, I can compare it to the description and see if it lines up.
Oh, yes, like that one you have there!
If it's anything like the bow, it'll be stored in a vault somewhere. Can you bring it to me? It'll really help with my research.
Alright, last piece of the puzzle. There's this special sword that I need. Made of shadow, or smoke or something. Nasty thing, wielded by something proper wicked.

The good news, is that I'm pretty sure it's not in a vault. The bad news is that I'm pretty sure it's in the possession of one of them enormous zogre thingies. You might need to kill quite a few of them to find it.
I... I'm just gonna sit here with me memories for a bit. You go on now, don't let an old git like me sour your mood. Thank you again, friend.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.

Quest_FH_GhostQuest.description: Help Zanik lay some spirits to rest by finding them and completing their unfinished business.

objectives.text: Find ghosts and complete their unfinished business. (0/3)
Find ghosts and complete their unfinished business. (1/3)
Find ghosts and complete their unfinished business. (2/3)
Return to Zanik.
Tell someone about these spirits.

dialogueRefs.text: Anything I can help with?
Thank you, I can feel them at peace, it's beautiful. The dead can get trapped in their issues, locked into a vicious cycle. You've stopped that.
OoooOOoooOOOOOooOOOOOoooOOOh!
OoooOOoooOOOOOooOOOOOoooOOOh!
OoooOOoooOOOOOooOOOOOoooOOOh!
Nothing interesting remains, just dust and old memories.
I couldn't tell you where exactly, but I've got an inkling. Like an itch on the inside of my nose, pointing the way -- yeah, it's horrible, please find them.
It's not as bad as it sounds, the Underworld. A bit grim, sure, but manageable. Imagine a city, full of the dead, waiting to pass on. That's what it is really.
I had a bit of a god's soul in me when I died, so my afterlife didn't go very well. Bandos was, after all, pretty upset with me.
Mostly, the dead are more than happy to cross over. This world can make you weary, and it's nice to finally have an excuse to rest. But a ghost doesn't get that.
Strange place this, isn't it? Not just the zombies and the horrible red pools of awfulness, there's a sadness to it too. A misery, like a chasm stretching across everything.
Once Imaru's influence has vanished completely, the restless spirits here can rest properly.
Oh, I'm so glad to have my sketch book back. I can't wait to draw everything around me. Now... where did I put a pencil?
Thank you, again. I just know that Edra would have loved it.
You already have this. You should return it to its owner.
There's a village, long since fallen to ruin. There waits a spirit shivering against the wind and rain.
Everyone just gets on with it. Similar to what it's like in the living world, only much less adventure.
His afterlife was, unsurprisingly, a world of constant battle. The strong crushed the weak on an endless cycle. I... I tried to protect them. I failed... a lot.

Some unfinished business keeps them trapped in place. Whether it be a mother desperately needing to know that her children are safe. Or some scholar who needs that elusive answer before they can let themselves sleep.
Strange place this, isn't it? Not just the zombies and the horrible red pools of awfulness, there's a sadness to it too. A misery, like a chasm stretching across everything.
The dead don't pass on here, not really. The tethers that hold them to their bodies are stretched and snap against Imaru's hunger. Then they're devoured like evening snacks.
I...I...I feel warm. I feel cosy. I feel like I'm home. Thank you, thank you friend. Now I can rest and move on once the dragon has been dealt with.
It's cold, don't you feel it? The wind feels like it's rushing through me, blowing away all the years I spent building this house.
Thank you for the shelter, even if it was short-lived. It was nice to be out of the cold, even for a little while.
I...I...I feel warm. I feel cosy. I feel like I'm home. Thank you, thank you friend. Now I can rest and move on once the dragon has been dealt with.
The afterlife is so dull, they don't tell you that in the books. Endless sameyness. Nothing changes. I want to yawn and yawn, but I can't even do that. No breath you see.
I just want to draw! Is that so much to ask? But my sketchbook is missing. My husband took it to work with him in the coal mine to the east. He likes to look at the pictures between swings.
I wonder how she's doing. Whether she managed to pass on safely. My granddaughter, Edra. She used to visit me often, always a smile on her face that could warm the coldest of winters.
Oh, if only I had a little doll to remember my darling Edra by. They were such lovely decorative things, made out of clay as I recall.
You find and old sketchbook, but your inventory is too full to collect it.
North of here, where the world rots away from the inside, a spirit clings to the world with memories of a loved one.

There's a great big river, the river Noumenon, that you can sail down on to whatever afterlife waits for you -- yeah, there's more than one. Each depending on your own beliefs. Or, if you're unlucky enough to be like me, the belief of the god's soul that's infected you.
It was to be an eternity of failure. Watching the innocent slain for no reason other than some brute's entertainment. Thankfully, a friend rescued me and I got a reprieve.
Some things are so important that they form a tether to our souls, that even Death's scythes can't cut. That's what a ghost is, a prisoner of ungiven closure.
The dead don't pass on here, not really. The tethers that hold them to their bodies are stretched and snap against Imaru's hunger. Then they're devoured like evening snacks.
Thank you, I can feel them at peace, it's beautiful. The dead can get trapped in their issues, locked into a vicious cycle. You've stopped that.

Still, there are some souls yet to pass on. Holding tight against Imaru's gluttony. I want to help them in these final moments, take the burdens from them so they can pass on once the dragon's power has fully waned.
Thank you!
I poured my life and soul into these foundations. Created a home for myself that I can be proud of. But now it's gone, and I feel like I'm lost without it.
I just want to draw! Is that so much to ask? But my sketchbook is missing. My husband took it to work with him in the coal mine to the east. He likes to look at the pictures between swings.
Every time she visited, I would give her a clay doll. A little figurine that she could paint and display with the others, like a little village of clay friends.
You find an old sketchbook.
Crumbling against decaying ruins, near a waterfall of grief, a ghost finds herself trapped with memories of a loved one. She needs something returned to her that has been buried in shadow.
I didn't enjoy Bandos' afterlife. I wouldn't recommend it.

Still, there are some souls yet to pass on. Holding tight against Imaru's gluttony. I want to help them in these final moments, take the burdens from them so they can pass on once the dragon's power has fully waned.
There are three lost souls all over Fellhollow, hidden in the remnants of human civilisation. Each one has something stopping them from finding peace.
Thank you for helping some of the spirits, but there are more still that need help finding peace. Please keep searching.
Once all this Imaru business is dealt with, then Death will be able to help them move on properly. In the mean time, here, something to say thank you.
Oh, you'll need an amulet of ghostspeak first. I think there was one in Brynmoor, all the way back. Lost in the village somewhere. You'll need to find it.
I just want four walls and a roof? Is that so much to ask? A little shelter against the cold?
But he never came back. I would have gone to look for him, but I got incinerated by a dragon. Which, you know, isn't ideal.
My sketchbook! You found it! Oh, I can't wait to draw in it again.
I wish I had one of those clay dolls to remember her by now. It would help me find peace in these turbulent times.
That doll! That clay figurine! It's just like the ones I made for my granddaughter. Would... would you be so kind as to give it to me? It would help me find peace.
Oh, you're already looking into that? I knew I could count on you!
As the ambassador to the underworld, I feel it's my duty to help these people out. Will you help me?
I miss him, sure, but I really miss my sketchbook. I've had decades to get over my grief, but the boredom lasts forever!
Thank you. There are three lost souls all over Fellhollow, hidden in the remnants of human civilisation. I feel them, like a warm fire in this cold dark place.
I understand. If you change your mind, or if you find one of them on your journey, please come back and see me.
Oh, yeah, husband. Err... he OK? Dead you say? Into a fine paste you say? Oh dear, how tragic. I'll... err... I'll go cry now I guess?
Thank you. Thank you so much. I can rest now. Well... once the devouring force has gone at least. Thank you again, my friend. You have made this old fool very happy.
I understand, hard to let go of these things. They are delightfully pretty, my granddaughter loves... no... loved them.
[Don't give the ghost a clay decoration.]
[Give the ghost a clay decoration.]
I'll talk to you later.
Not right now.
Yes.
Ask where the ghosts are.
Ask about the Underworld.
Ask about the Afterlife.
Ask about ghosts.

Quest_FH_MirrorMirror.description: Help free a mysterious figure from their mirror prison.

objectives.text: Gather dragon blood, spectral silver thread and a ritual spellbook and bring them back to the mirror.
Rekindle the memorial candles across Ashenfall.
Speak to the mirror.

dialogueRefs.text: A mysterious spellbook, from Agatha's Magical Delivery Service.
Wait! A person? An actual, real life person and not some shambling nightmare picking rubbish out of its teeth? Hello! Hello! Oh, also, help?
Hello?

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. You stare into the mirror, guilt finally quelling the rage that always burns in your chest. The nightmare all around you, your fault, but who will punish you, if not yourself?
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. You've grown to like the antipoison's taste, a pick-me-up first thing in the morning. The cave is damp, but oddly comforting. The bodies of seven garou keep you warm  as they burn. You wonder if you have a future in potions.
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. Your pour your rage into the heavens, corrupting the veil a god placed there to protect. Dark magic turns clouds into weapons, blasting settlements with spears of lightning. You laugh, a cold and bitter sound, at the nightmare you've wrought.
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. Your fingers are warm, though his body grows colder with each second. There is no breath in his lungs and once bright eyes are cold and empty. A sorrow like no other grasps icy fingers around your heart and mercy dies to its frigid touch.
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. A shared meal, tougher than it should be. A monster avoided through quick wit and guile. A silent conversation worth more than a thousand words.
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

The soul ignites the candle. A memory that is not yours seeps into your thoughts. Distrustful eyes fall upon you. Scorn and derision from every corner. The priests shake their head at you. Only one face smiles back beneath a mask of bone.
No flame seems to touch this wick, as though it burns from something else.

A... horrible necromancer trapped me in this mirror decades ago. Punishment for all my mistakes. I'm not saying I didn't deserve it, but it's been... well, an eternity, and I think I've served my time.
She even gave me the ritual to release myself to...err... taunt me, yes, taunt me. It's quite simple to resolve, really, it shouldn't take long.
You have no room in your inventory for this book, you'll need to make some space and come back to it later.

I just need you to grab a few things. Dragon blood, which should be plentiful. A copy of the spell from my old shop in Emberwood's windmill, and some spectral silver thread - my seamstress, Edna, can help you there.
A mote of light runs between yourself and the skeleton and she turns her skull to face you and opens her arms out wide, expectantly.
I'll need you to rekindle my memories, quite literally.
I just need you to grab a few things, so I can get myself out of this mirror.
The mistress needssss...bring me a bar of silver, a spool of fine thread, a bottle of sacred oil, and six soul fragments and I shall weave what she needsssss.

When one lives as long as I have, one's memories get a little overcrowded and sometimes you just need to put them somewhere for safekeeping. I've left a few of mine as "memorial candles" in each region I've visited.
I need dragon blood, it's the blood of the enemy and that always has mystical significance. I read about it in a book once.
A mote of light runs between yourself and the skeleton and she turns her skull to face you and opens her arms out wide, expectantly.

For each candle you light, you'll rekindle a memory which will help me reconnect myself to this world and pull myself back through. I'll give you a spark to reignite them, just a small piece of my soul so the candles will ignite when you find them.
*A small greenish flame passes from the mirror and into the palm of your hand. It feels full of sorrow, rage and boundless grief.*

Spectral silver thread will help me stitch the mirror back together. My seamstress, Edna, can help you there. You can find her little cottage in the centre of Dragon's Run. She's...err... quite thin these days.
Great, that's all the bits I need! Thank you so much... I'll take those off your hands for now, just press them to the glass. It's weird, I know, but it won't hurt.
Oh, that you already have!
The skeleton returns to rest, leaving you without your thread.

Finally I need a copy of the spell itself. Using morse code and a very clever pigeon, I managed to order a copy from Agatha's mail-order magic -- but it got sent back to my shop, in my windmill in Emberwood village.
Great, that's all the bits I need! Thank you so much... I'll take those off your hands for now, just press them to the glass. It's weird, I know, but it won't hurt.
You have no room to take thisss thread. Return to me when space is made among your belongings.
The skeleton performs a series of gestures, too quick and strange for your eyes to follow and then hands you a spool of spectral silver thread. The skeleton returns to rest.
Brilliant stuff! I can get the spell going now. I should be out of here in... what... a week or so.
Wonderful, I can start getting the ritual ready on my end. I just need something to tether myself back to your side of reality. I'll need you to rekindle my memories, quite literally.
Well, there's nothing I can do until you give me the ingredients. Don't worry, I'll be right here until you change your mind... right...here...

What? You don't need to stick around for that, I'm good now. I can stitch this mirror back together and then escape this reflective prison. You've done everything I need.

For each candle you light, you'll rekindle a memory which will help me reconnect myself to this world and pull myself back through. I'll give you a spark to reignite them, just a small piece of my soul so the candles will ignite when you find them.

Here, take this as a thank you. Who knows, we might see each other on the other side sometime. Your side, I mean, not this one... that wasn't a threat, we're cool.

Quest_FH_NightoftheSpectralBoom.displayName: Things That Go Boom In The Night
Quest_FH_NightoftheSpectralBoom.description: Gather spectral chinchompa skulls so that Vannaka can help the land heal.

objectives.text: Gather 10 spectral chinchompa skulls and bring them to Vannaka in Fellhollow.
Speak to Vannaka in Fellhollow.

dialogueRefs.text: Young pup, it seems like the spirits here are in dire trouble and I'll need a little more of your help to put things right.
I see you've been hunting more of those spiritual pests. Nasty creatures those, best to get rid of them. Here, I'll take those skulls off your hands and give you something for your efforts.
I see you've gathered a few more of those skulls, gather a few more and come back to me I'll reward you for every ten you find.
It'll take some time for the land to heal, but when it does it'll remember the good work you've done for it. The land always remembers.
The land is angry. Enraged at the corruption forced upon it and in turn it fights back. Dangerous spirits of destruction roam this land in the fluffiest of forms.
You've earned a rest, but if you're looking for work come back and see me. I have another task I could use your help with.
Chinchompas. Ghostly little critters with explosive personalities. They threaten our efforts here, as the land does not understand we work in its interest.
Here, something for your hard work. It's not much, young pup, but it'll be a reminder of the good work you've done for this place.
Find those chinchompa spirits and put an end to them before they can put an end to you. If they explode, their essence will just reform somewhere else, so strike them before they can.
Or I would, if you weren't so overburdened. Clear some space, young pup, then come find me.
It is the vet's hand that the dog bites most, after all. I need you to find these critters and hunt down as many as you can, before they explode and rip the land apart in the process.
In time, thanks to this, and with Imaru's destruction, we may see the land return to the lush land it once was. In a few decades perhaps.
If you bring me their skulls, I can do what I can to help lay their spirits to rest. Perhaps we can curb some of this land's fury.
If you bring me ten of their skulls, I can do what I can to help lay their spirits to rest. Perhaps we can curb some of this land's fury.
If you find more of them, bring them to me. I'll take ten at a time, clear the problem up faster that way.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
Hrmm, what do you have there young pup? The spectral skulls of vengeful little spirits? I know what this means.
You've got enough there for me to sort this mess out. An old ritual, primal and primordial nonsense -- not my favourite thing to work with, but needs must.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
Here, something for your hard work. It's not much, young pup, but it'll be a reminder of the good work you've done for this place.

objectives.text: Find five of Abraxus’ missing books in eastern Fellhollow and return them to him.
Bring the books to Abraxus.
Defeat Abraxus' enemies to retrieve the scrolls.
Bring the scrolls to Abraxus.
Find five of Abraxus’ missing books in eastern Fellhollow and return them to him.
Defeat Abraxus' enemies to retrieve the scrolls. Then return them to Abraxus.
Find the owner of the sinister text.

dialogueRefs.text: You find one of Abraxus' books.
You find one of Abraxus' books.
You find one of Abraxus' books.
You find one of Abraxus' books.
You find one of Abraxus' books.
You find one of Abraxus' scrolls. The writing crawls along the page making it impossible to read without strange arcane knowledge.
You find one of Abraxus' scrolls. Each time you look at the scroll, you could swear the text is different to the last time you looked.
You find one of Abraxus' scrolls. It's too awful, you cannot bring yourself to read it.
Now, if you'll excuse me, I need to mail a pebble to my... to an old friend of mine. See if that will let me haunt them for a while. I am so bored of this view.
Among all the technical jargon, a note falls out.
The book is written in the language of Infernus and impossible to read. However, a perfumed note is stuffed between the pages...
This book appears to be a grimoire of terrible curses. When you open it a crumpled note falls out.
This book appears to be a religious dissertation on the merits of the Zamorak faith. When you open it a letter falls out.
This tome writhes beneath your fingertips, as if infused with some dread spirit. It practically spits a letter out at you.
What do you want? I have little time for the likes of you. Only a member of my own order can assist me and you certainly don't look the part.
OoooOOooOOoooOooooOoooh!

On summer days, with bluer skies,
I am oft reminded of your eyes. 
In winter nights, by the fire we roast,
And I think about what I love the most.
My dearest Abraxus, this keep is full of madmen and morons. People to whom power means strength and might, rather than unraveling the secrets of the universe.
You make me so angry Abraxus. A fire I cannot put out. I want to shout at you. I want to kick you down the stairs. I want to wrap my arms around you and scream into your chest.
Dear Abraxus, I hope this letter finds you well. Dowdun Reach is proving both fascinating and infuriating in equal measure.
Dear Valerius, I am too cowardly to send this letter. Too afraid that you might burn it, or laugh at it, or worse still, ignore it. But if I do not say it now, I never will.
Ah, apprentice... I assume you're an apprentice, with robes that shabby what else could you be? Still, needs must. Apprentice, I require your assistance.

It's your sparkling wit, your wicked smile.
With your every word, you do beguile.
We are looking to create a demonic portal, that we might summon beings from another world. Imagine! We could learn so much!
You make me a very undignified wizard, Abraxus. Very undignified indeed.
Whilst we are not limited by the prattling sensibilities of the village wizards, they replace it with a sort of blind aggression and anger against everyone.
*The letter is torn in half before any more can be said.*
Yes, yes, I know, I know. You stand in the presence of Abraxus the Eternal, master of necromancy. Keeper of secrets both occult and arcane.
*Great scratch marks of pencil obscure the rest of the page.*
Yet they will just try and raise an army. Urgh! How I wish you were here with me. We could show them what a real wizard can do.
Still, I do wish you would join me. I think you might find there are wonderful secrets to uncover when one is not shackled by pointless morality.
You are very blessed, I am sure. Now, I need you to assist me. My library has been ransacked by the locals and my most precious tomes spread across the eastern parts of this region.
Find them, all five of them, bring them to me and -- this is crucial -- do not read them. Your mind is too young, too limited to contain the dread secrets within! Well... hop to it!
Three of my secret scrolls have been stolen and you must reclaim them for me.
The first was stolen by a wretched green dragon known as Blightscale. Arrogant creature, you must make a lesson of her hubris.
In disguise are we? Blending in with the riff raff and the yobs? Not sure I agree with such a plan, but you do you.
I need you to find my books. Find them, all five of them, bring them to me and -- this is crucial -- do not read them. Your feeble mind cannot handle their secrets.
OoooOOooOOoooOooooOoooh!
You have done well my apprentice and earned something no one else has earned in centuries -- my respect.
The second scroll was taken by a zogre known as Ulgo. Foul creature, stinks beyond comprehension, but I'm sure you can handle it.
I need you to find my books. Find them, all five of them, bring them to me and -- this is crucial -- do not read them. Your feeble mind cannot handle their secrets.
But I am not fool enough to believe you would find such a thing sufficient for your efforts, so, here, take this instead. May it serve you well.
The last was taken by a rival of mine, Razlem - the deranged. A far less skilled necromancer than myself, but dangerous none the less.
Now, if you'll excuse me, I need to mail a pebble to my... to an old friend of mine. See if that will let me haunt them for a while. I am so bored of this view.
Excellent, excellent, you've found my books. I will trust you were not fool enough to peak.
Oh, but you already have my books. Are you in league with the thief, perhaps? Or are you simply more efficient than expected. No matter, your work is appreciated.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
However, your assistance is still required, apprentice. Three of my secret scrolls have been stolen and you must reclaim them for me.
