Quest_FH_WitherBeast.description: Help Vannaka safeguard Fellhollow's nature spirits, by hunting them down, in willow groves, and collecting their hearts.

objectives.text: Hunt down Nature Spirits near Fellhollow's willow groves and bring three of their hearts to Vannaka.
Bring the hearts to Vannaka.
Bring the Primordial Heart to someone with an interest in the wild hunt.

dialogueRefs.text: Young pup, it seems like the spirits here are in dire trouble and I'll need a little more of your help to put things right.
I see you've been hunting more of those spiritual pests. Nasty creatures those, best to get rid of them. Here, I'll take those skulls off your hands and give you something for your efforts.
I see you've gathered a few more of those skulls, gather a few more and come back to me I'll reward you for every ten you find.
It'll take some time for the land to heal, but when it does it'll remember the good work you've done for it. The land always remembers.
The land is angry. Enraged at the corruption forced upon it and in turn it fights back. Dangerous spirits of destruction roam this land in the fluffiest of forms.
You've earned a rest, but if you're looking for work come back and see me. I have another task I could use your help with.
Chinchompas. Ghostly little critters with explosive personalities. They threaten our efforts here, as the land does not understand we work in its interest.
Here, something for your hard work. It's not much, young pup, but it'll be a reminder of the good work you've done for this place.
Find those chinchompa spirits and put an end to them before they can put an end to you. If they explode, their essence will just reform somewhere else, so strike them before they can.
Or I would, if you weren't so overburdened. Clear some space, young pup, then come find me.
It is the vet's hand that the dog bites most, after all. I need you to find these critters and hunt down as many as you can, before they explode and rip the land apart in the process.
In time, thanks to this, and with Imaru's destruction, we may see the land return to the lush land it once was. In a few decades perhaps.
If you bring me their skulls, I can do what I can to help lay their spirits to rest. Perhaps we can curb some of this land's fury.
If you bring me ten of their skulls, I can do what I can to help lay their spirits to rest. Perhaps we can curb some of this land's fury.
If you find more of them, bring them to me. I'll take ten at a time, clear the problem up faster that way.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
Hrmm, what do you have there young pup? The spectral skulls of vengeful little spirits? I know what this means.
You've got enough there for me to sort this mess out. An old ritual, primal and primordial nonsense -- not my favourite thing to work with, but needs must.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
Here, something for your hard work. It's not much, young pup, but it'll be a reminder of the good work you've done for this place.
Hello there, young pup, what can I help you with?
Not a pleasant landscape this, ey, young pup? Life is fading, drained away by a dragon's hunger. Rotten creatures, dragons.
Not a pleasant landscape this, ey, young pup? Life is fading, drained away by a dragon's hunger. Rotten creatures, dragons.
Even this willow grove, once home to a proud and magnificent nature spirit, is now corrupted by wither and rot. That poor spirit has withered away to nothing.
You did it, well done. Now, the tricky part. I asked you to get these hearts because of a garou ritual I learned. An old one, from their time before Kuldra.
Majestic creatures, aren't they? I'm sure it feels strange to have to hunt them, but trust me we're doing them a favour. You're part way there, but I'll need more hearts.

Look for willow groves, like this one, those are places where nature spirits thrive. There's a few to the west of here. Bring me three of their hearts and we can find a way to keep them safe from this withering hunger.
Even this willow grove, once home to a proud and magnificent nature spirit, is now corrupted by wither and rot. That poor spirit has withered away to nothing.
If this land is ever going to heal, we need to save the rest of those spirits and the only way to save them, is to hunt them and kill them.
How are you and your new friend getting on? Running wild and free, I hope. See, you did them a favour by hunting them here. Now they're safe from this land's blighted curse.
It's a way to liberate the spirit from this place. Allow it to run free and wild, bound to a new anchor, one able to give them freedom.

Look for willow groves, those are places where nature spirits thrive. There's a few to the west of here. Bring me the spirits' hearts and we can find a way to keep them safe from this withering hunger.
If this land is ever going to heal, we need to save the rest of those spirits and the only way to save them, is to hunt them and kill them.
Don't worry, they're meant to be hunted. That's the spirit way, a spirit of nature should be hunted by a predator, not slowly drained away by a monster, and you're the apex predator here.
You and your spirit friend seem happy together, young pup. Always good to see that sort of bond between man and beast.
You and your spirit friend seem happy together, young pup. Always good to see that sort of bond between man and beast.
That anchor is you. Now, one moment and... here... that should do it. With a little magic, that spirit will carry you across Ashenfall. Give it a good run, won't you?

You'll be doing this place a favour by hunting them, trust me. Look for willow groves, like this one, those are places where nature spirits thrive. Bring me three of their hearts and we can find a way to keep them safe from this withering hunger.

Ah, but I see you've been liberating more nature spirits. Good work. It may feel strange, but you're doing them a favour, trust me. Tell you what, bring me three of them and I'll give you some of those shiny stones Death seems so interested in.
You've gathered another three hearts for me from the nature spirits? Good, very good. You're a skilled hunter, young pup, you should be proud.
Ah... but your a skilled hunter, young pup, I see you've already gathered them.
I see you're part way there already. Just need to get the rest and we can help this spirit escape Imaru's foul curse.
I'll take them off your hands and you can take these in their place. Shiny little stones that old Harold loves so much.
Ah, or I would give them to you if you had any room. Make some space and then come back and talk to me.
Ask about nature spirits.
Ask about spectral chinchompas.

Quest_FH_WitherWard.description: Find the statues to gain entrance to the vault and uncover the secrets that lie within.

objectives.text: Access the vault and find the hidden secret within.
Bring the dwarven writing to Doric.
Find someone in Fellhollow that can translate dwarvish text.

dialogueRefs.text: Thanks for all your help. Ashenfall really is home to some remarkable weapons. I wonder what else we'll uncover? My boy, Boric, would love this place.
You know what, we make a good team, you and I. You find me things and I record them for future crafters to enjoy.
It may not sound like much, but sharing knowledge is what turns a gathering of people into a thriving community.
You know what, we make a good team, you and I. You find me things and I record them for future crafters to enjoy.
Amazing, you've got the staff! That's... that's exactly like the story... this is... hrmm. Why would this story be so accurate, unless...
I'm looking for a necromancer's staff. Perhaps it's another weapon in one of those dragonkin vaults?
Well now, there you have it! A shadow sword!
We're looking for a shadow sword. When I was investigating the area the clues I found pointed to one of those zogre things. You might need to kill quite a few of them.
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
I'm looking for an undead ranger's bow. Perhaps it's another weapon in one of those dragonkin vaults?
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
That's it! That's the bow! It looks just like the story described. I wonder...
It's all like the story. You know, I used to tell my boy this story, good old Boric. He was so excited to hear the tale of heroic warriors and undead monsters.
Ah, yes, you must be quite busy. Well, I won't keep you. If you're bored later, come say hi.
Wonderful. Now then, I once told me lad about this strange warrior from far away. Fought great evil, undead beasties and the like.
Wonderful. Now then, I once told me lad about this strange warrior from far away. Fought great evil, undead beasties and the like.
Ah, yes, you must be quite busy. Well, I won't keep you. If you're bored later, come say hi.
Here, my little way of saying thank you.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
To think, I'm standing in the very land this story took place. Boric would love to hear this... if... if I ever get a chance to see him again of course.
Sounds familiar, doesn't it? A land full of the undead, with deadly monsters roaming around. I'm now wondering if the story came from here somehow.
Sounds familiar, doesn't it? A land full of the undead, with deadly monsters roaming around. I'm now wondering if the story came from here somehow.
Here, a little something for your troubles.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
Ah don't mind me. Just a melancholic old man worried about his fully grown and perfectly capable boy. I just don't tell him enough how proud of him I am.
As the tale goes, the warrior first had to face off against a deadly archer. All bone and dark magic. Had this skeletal bow that was described in eerie detail.
As the tale goes, the warrior first had to face off against a deadly archer. All bone and dark magic. Had this skeletal bow that was described in eerie detail.
OK, let's look at the next part of the story. There was a necromancer, nasty piece of work, with a powerful magic staff.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
Anyway, here, have this. My little way of saying thank you for helping an old codger like me connect to happy memories.
If you can find and make me that undead ranger's bow, I can compare it to the description and see if it lines up.
Oh, yes, like that one you have there!
If it's anything like the bow, it'll be stored in a vault somewhere. Can you bring it to me? It'll really help with my research.
Alright, last piece of the puzzle. There's this special sword that I need. Made of shadow, or smoke or something. Nasty thing, wielded by something proper wicked.

The good news, is that I'm pretty sure it's not in a vault. The bad news is that I'm pretty sure it's in the possession of one of them enormous zogre thingies. You might need to kill quite a few of them to find it.
I... I'm just gonna sit here with me memories for a bit. You go on now, don't let an old git like me sour your mood. Thank you again, friend.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
I've got a little something to thank you for your efforts so far, but you seem a bit overburdened. I'll hold on to it til you've got your hands a bit freer.
I'm listening
Maybe later
I'm listening
Maybe later
The door is sealed by Dragonkin magic.
You hear the sound of a dragonkin lock releasing.
The statue has no further secrets for you.
I don't like this place, it's creepy and weird. Had to whack several zombies with my hammer and now it's got this weird purple ooze on it that won't wash off.
Taken a look in that locked vault yet? There must be a trick to it. Those dragonkin were a smart lot, secretive... and arrogant as heck.
Well, will you look at that, another dwarven tablet. Why were the dragonkin out here stealing dwarven secrets?
Still, I'm betting there's something interesting waiting around here. There are vaults in this place and they must be loaded with dragonkin secrets.
You find strange dwarven writings that you cannot read. Perhaps Doric can translate for you.
If you can find your way inside, let me know if you discover anything interesting.
I guess we'll never know. Here, let me translate this for you, hopefully it'll help you on your travels.

Who knows what you might find? I discovered one vault, and I was all geared up to visit, but it's locked down tight. Hey, I know, if you get a chance why don't you take a look? Let me know what you find inside.

Well now, that is unexpected. This is the Salve amulet... why is this here? It requires a gemstone only found by the river Salve back in Misthalin. I mean, it's handy against the undead, so it'll be real useful here.
You find strange dwarven writings that you cannot read. Perhaps someone can translate for you.

Oh! Ha, you're gonna laugh at this, but I actually have one of them river Salve gemstones. I found one a few years back and I just keep it with me as a good luck charm. Here, you should take it, make yourself one of those salve amulets.
Oh, you don't appear to have the space for it. Come back and see me when you do.

objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man in Bramblemead village.

dialogueRefs.text: Good, you've got the basics under your belt, but now the guide ropes are off. Taking down a dragon won't be easy, but you've got the skills you need to do it. Well... almost.
We need to start thinking long term. Bramblemead village is an excellent place for an outpost, even if it's a little overrun with goblins right now.
Not finished yet? The longer you leave things, the more likely you are to become a dragon's dinner.
Good, you've built a shelter. I mean... it could do with some work, we're gonna be here a while. Have you considered the decor at all?
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
Maybe some better lighting? Curtains? A single potted plant? *Sigh* no, no, you're right. It's not important. Why live it up when there's so much squalor to enjoy?
Doesn't need to be fancy -- though style is always worth pursuing -- but it needs to be functional. Make a shelter, some foundations, walls, and a roof, and then build and claim a bed in it.
Doesn't need to be fancy -- though style is always worth pursuing -- but it needs to be functional. Make a shelter, some foundations, walls, and a roof, and then build and claim a bed in it.
Anyway, look, we're set up here, but there's one of our number missing. Young Cathan, an adventurer in training that came along with us.
You can go bigger, of course, let your inner architect run wild, but the bed's the bare minimum we need to get started. Go on, hop to it. Get!
You can go bigger, of course, let your inner architect run wild, but the bed's the bare minimum we need to get started. Go on, hop to it. Get!
He disappeared after we got the lodestone working, vanished before you arrived. I'd like to track him down. To do that I need to cast a locator spell.
I'm just missing one ingredient, which I'll need from you. Antlers. You can get them from deer, hunt one and bring me the antlers. Then we'll get started. But first, here, take this.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
Hrmm?
Ah, hello there.
Aren't you helping the others out? What are you talking to me for? Check your map if you're not sure what you're meant to be doing.
You've dealt with the problem for now, but who knows what danger waits around the corner? If I were you, I'd get yourself ready for whatever horribleness is coming next.
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.

Now then, an adventurer's work is never finished. Trust me, I know. There's a strange door to the north, just past Ashien's Watch and it's sending chills down my spine. Meet me there, we'll talk more.
Ask about fishing.
Ask about Farming
<Hand over Velgar's head>
<Refuse to hand over Velgar's head>
Ask about fishing.
Ask about Farming
Is there anything I can help with?
Ask about the Dragon Slayer quest.
Welcome to Ashenfall, sorry about the mess. Had a bit of a dragon problem, that's why we've called for you.
You've come at a great time. Heroic opportunities await. This long-forgotten place is just screaming to be explored.
Strange place this. Ashenfall, I mean. Could make a real home here, if things stopped trying to kill us.
But before all that, how about we take you through some survival basics?
Gathering resources and crafting items, that's the basics of survival in this place. Seek out new resources to discover new recipes.
Oh dear, you just walked right past the Wise Old Man. He won't like that. Best go back and say hi, eh?
Me? Name's Doric. I'm just a stupid old blacksmith that got swept up in tales of adventure. Trying to win back me glory days.
It's a wild place this. Beasties everywhere, and no civilisation in sight. Just the remnants, ghosts of the past.
Left my son behind to watch the shop. Good lad, gonna do good things. Hope he's not too worried about his dad.
But you see that great tower, off in the distance? That's dragonkin that is. Means there's probably stuff worth finding about this place.
You'll want to get to grips with gathering and crafting first, Doric can help you with that.
Fair enough, I do like someone that can show initiative.
Ah, but you've got a good head on yer shoulders. I see you've already got some water, so you won't die of thirst.
Aye, that's a fine club you got there, but even the best weapons break over time. When that happens use a crafting bench to repair your gear.
Still, no point lollygagging around. I'll catch my breath and then explore these new lands. Who knows? Might find something.
You'll find him outside the temple. Check your map if you get lost, but he should be easy to spot.
But not here. Come find me in Bramblemead Village, and we'll get you started.
Still, it's going to be tough surviving this place with a dragon about.
By Saradomin's big bushy beard! Just our luck, a great ruddy dragon. Think it were him that got the others - may they rest in peace.
Ah good, you've got some water. Bit dirty, I know, but better than nothing. Be careful though, the water's tainted and it'll make life difficult if you drink too much.
Now you've got something to fight with, go chat to Vannaka over to the north east, he can teach you how to keep fighting fit.
Oh, you made a dagger, not a club? Aye, it's a nice piece of work, not what I asked for, but that's fine.
You'll want to build yourself a crafting table. Then once you've done that craft yourself a stone club.
He's the only dwarf on the continent, that we know of anyway, can't miss him.
And look at ya! Not a knife to yer name, no, no, we can't be doing with that. Come on, let's get you prepared. You need to go and craft a stone club.
But look at you, all skin and bones. Must be proper parched after a journey like that.
Zanik says boiling it sorts it all out. So might want to give that a look later, when you've got a chance. Anyway, time we got you all set up to survive this harsh land.
I've marked two ponds on your map, to the northwest and south of us. Grab some water from there and bring it back here. Then I'll teach you what you'll need to survive.
Ah, good, you've got some nice clean water there. The water in lakes and rivers tends to be dirty, tainted by something nasty that will make life difficult if you drink too much.
Before you go, here, something to help you on your way.
Now, even the best weapons break over time. When that happens use a crafting bench to repair your gear.
Both require stone and ash logs, which you'll find scattered all over the ground around here.
It won't kill a dragon, but it's better than nothing and it'll help you live a bit longer, giving you time to make something better.
Dehydration and starvation are deadlier than dragons, so you're going to need keep an eye on your basic needs, like hunger and thirst.
And look at ya! Not a knife to yer name, no, no, we can't be doing with that. Come on, let's get you prepared. You need to go and craft a stone club.
You'll need to gather stone and ash logs, which you can find laying around, then you'll want to build a crafting table to craft the club.
I've marked two ponds on your map, to the northwest and south of us. Grab some water from there and bring it back here. Then I'll teach you what you'll need to survive.
It won't kill a dragon, but it's better than nothing and it'll help you live a bit longer, giving you time to make something better.
Oh dear, you seem a little overburdened at the moment. Come and see me when you've got some space free in your backpack.
Oh, I'm Doric by the way. Resident blacksmith and craftsperson on this expedition. Nice to meet you. Now, stop standing around and go make that club!
If you see a redberry bush along the way, grab yourself a handful. Not much of a meal, but a little food is better than no food at all.
You'll need to gather stone and ash logs, which you can find laying around, then you'll want to build a crafting table to craft the club.
Oh, I'm Doric by the way. Resident blacksmith and craftsperson on this expedition. Nice to meet you. Now, stop standing around and go make that club!
Yes please [Begin Tutorial]
I can work it out [Skip Tutorial]
Who are you?
Can you tell me about Ashenfall?
There are secrets hidden all over Ashenfall, I'm sure of it. Look around, explore, and see what you can find.
I think someone is looking for you. Mentioned a task they needed you to complete. Check your map for where to find them.
Vannaka was looking for you, mentioned something about fine dining?
Right, now that you've learned the basics, it's time to get started. The Wise Old Man is waiting for you just outside Bramblemead Village. Follow your compass to find him.
Better not keep him waiting too long, he gets real cranky.
Great work! Runes are the lifeblood of magic, you'll need them to cast spells and use magic staves. A well placed spell can make all the difference.
Not made the runes yet? You'll need to mine essence from the floating geysers and then craft air and astral runes either by building a rune altar or by siphoning from nearby Anima Vents.
You'll unlock new spells as you improve your skills. Here, this book should help you toward that. Have a play around with them, you'll find they can be incredibly useful.
Right, now that you've learned the basics, it's time to get started. The Wise Old Man is waiting for you just outside Bramblemead Village. Follow your compass to find him.
Better not keep him waiting too long, he gets real cranky.
Oh wow, bit of a packrat are we? You're carrying too much right now, come back and chat with me when you've cleared some space from your backpack.

Quest_FTUE_Farming.description: Learn the basics of the Farming skill from the Wise Old Man.

objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man, in Bramblemead, to learn about the Farming skill.
[TEMP] Build a Garden Plot
[TEMP] Plant Wheat Seeds

dialogueRefs.text: What would you like to know?
Anything else I can help you with?
Oh? You've overburdened yourself with all the random things you can cram in your pockets. Come back and see me when you've made a bit of room.
Look at you, practically master farmer already. Farming is a wonderful way to keep yourself well fed, and with access to useful materials.
First, you'll need to build a farming plot. Use a spade on it to clear it of weeds. Once it's completely clear, you're ready to plant.
Plants are like people, they need water to survive. You'll want to keep your plants nice and hydrated, so that they don't succumb to disease.
Compost improves the yield on your crops when you harvest them. They simply love to spread their roots around in the stinky stuff.
I see you've started to get a little green around the thumbs! Farming will make survival on Ashenfall a little less horrible.
Oh? You've overburdened yourself with all the random things you can cram in your pockets. Come back and see me when you've made a bit of room.
Speaking of useful, here, take this. My little gift to you. Just don't tell the others, they'll get all jealous again.
Just grab the seeds in your hand, and then whack em into the soil. No need for grace, or ceremony, just whomp them in and they'll be fine.
Grab yourself a watering can, fill it with water at a water source, and then liberally douse your patch until it's fully soaked through.
To make compost, you'll first need to build a Compost Bin. Then you'll want to fill it with compostible ingredients, like weeds, unwanted logs or irritating exes.
You'll be able to grow fruits, vegetables, and all manner of plants. Food, potion ingredients and perhaps some crafting resources too!
Make sure to water your plants every day, ideally first thing in the morning, to keep them nice and healthy.
Give it a little time for the newly added stuff to rot down into compost and then take a Compost Bucket and fill it up.
Why don't you go and give it a proper go right now? Go harvest some crops and then come back and see me. I'll give you a little something for your efforts.
Then just pour the contents of your bucket over the farming plot, making sure it's spread over it as fully as possible.
Here, take these to get you started.
Oh? You've overburdened yourself with all the random things you can cram in your pockets. Come back and see me when you've made a bit of room.
Ask about planting seeds.
Ask about watering plants.
Ask about compost.
I have no more questions.

I wonder why they're not in the history books.
Dragons, it had to be dragons. Oh, hi, sorry, nice to meet you, I'm Zanik. I'm the local survival and goblin expert around here.
I'm regretting it a bit, what with big scary dragons and all, but I'm excited too. Looking forward to learn everything about this place.
As well as goblins, look at the creatures here. So vibrant and full of life. This whole place feels... magical.
The interesting thing about Ashenfall is that it's laced with magic. Anima everywhere, pouring out of the ground. Which we can use to our advantage.
Cut down trees and gather 50 ash logs, then bring them to me.
Great, you've got them. Now, between you and me, that was a bit repetitive right? I'd be exhausted having to do that all the time.
Here, I'll show you. First, let's look at things without magic to help you. I need you to cut down a couple of trees and bring me some ash logs. Simple, right?
Fortunately, we've got magic! As you improve in a skill you'll discover spells that you can use, such as my favourite - Axtral Projection.
About fifty ash logs should do it, so make sure you've got a well maintained axe. Shouldn't take too long, come back to me when you have them.
Axtral projection will let you slice down trees with a wave of your fingers. Much less time consuming than the lumberjack gig.
But, magic comes at a cost -- runes. You'll need both air and astral runes to cast Axtral projection, so here's how to get them.

Who are you?
Can you tell me about Ashenfall?

Getting ahead of yourself, aren't we, young pup? Check your map to see where you're meant to be headed.
My name is Vannaka and back on the mainland I was a Slayer Master. It was my job to send adventurers after dangerous beasts.
Be ready to fight, that's my first piece of advice. Craft armour, weapons and anything else you need for battle.
Well met, young pup. Looking to get yourself ready to face off against a dragon? You'll need more than that butter knife to kill one, but you've got to start somewhere.
Well met, young pup. Looking to get yourself ready to face off against a dragon? You'll need more than that potato masher to kill one, but you've got to start somewhere.
Cull the population of monsters, to make the world a better place.
There are goblins everywhere in Bramblemead and deadlier things beyond.

Behind me, up that little hill, is a windmill infested with rats. I want you to kill some of them and cook their meat.

objectives.text: Speak to Zanik.
Build and then claim a bed.
Speak to Zanik.

dialogueRefs.text: Why not expand your shelter and turn it into a proper home? You could add rooms, floors, really make something of it.
Hi there. It's good to see new blood, hope you're ready to brave this place. I think Doric needs your attention, best say hi.
You must be the newbie. I'm Zanik, it's a pleasure to meet you.
Not finished yet? Once you've made a shelter, make sure you've claimed a bed. Then come back and see me.
I see you've got yourself all set up now, great work!
Ashenfall's a harsh place to live in, you're gonna need a shelter and somewhere to rest.
Death's made a deal with the Wise Old Coot, so if you die you'll just find yourself in your bed again. Handy right?
Make yourself a shelter out of wood and stone. Any building will do, just needs floors, walls and a roof. When building, be sure to keep your structure stable.
I imagine you've been seeing your skills grow stronger. As you level up, you'll unlock special spells to make surviving here easier.
Then make and claim a bed to rest in. To make a bed you're going to need something soft, like fur. Look around for small creatures to get fur from.
To cast spells you're going to need to learn about runes. The Wise Old Man can help you with that.
When you've done all that come back and see me. I'll give you something to help you on your journey.

Quest_FTUE_Q4.description: Learn the basics of crafting runes.

objectives.text: Speak to the Wise Old Man in the temple.
Mine rune essence, build a rune altar and craft some air runes.
Speak to the Wise Old Man in the temple.

dialogueRefs.text: Aren't you helping the others out? What are you talking to me for? Check your map if you're not sure what you're meant to be doing.

Runes, right? Thousands of years ago Guthix created special stones containing magical power. Runes.
You've crafted some runes I see, good. Magic is a tool, just like any other, but one worth keeping around.
Not made any runes yet? It's quite simple really, you just need to find a source of rune essence.
Runes are made from rune essence, a special kind of stone that absorbs and holds magical power - anima.
You'll discover several spells as you improve your skills. Try experimenting with all of them. Magic is fun!
There's a deposit of essence behind this temple. Go mine it, then build yourself a rune altar. You might want to get yourself a pickaxe.
There's a deposit of essence behind this temple. Go mine it, then build yourself a rune altar. You might want to get yourself a pickaxe.
Now, onto the scary stuff. You'll want to talk to Vannaka next. He'll help you avoid a brutal and agonising death...maybe. Have fun!
When you've done that, craft yourself some air runes at the altar.

objectives.text: Speak to Vannaka.

Kill rats and successfully cook one rat roast from their meat.

We need to start thinking long term. Bramblemead village is an excellent place for an outpost, even if it's a little overrun with goblins right now.
Not finished yet? The longer you leave things, the more likely you are to become a dragon's dinner.
Good, you've built a shelter. I mean... it could do with some work, we're gonna be here a while. Have you considered the decor at all?
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
We should build our new base of operations here. By we, I mean you -- bad back.
Maybe some better lighting? Curtains? A single potted plant? *Sigh* no, no, you're right. It's not important. Why live it up when there's so much squalor to enjoy?
Doesn't need to be fancy -- though style is always worth pursuing -- but it needs to be functional. Make a shelter, some foundations, walls, and a roof, and then build and claim a bed in it.

You can go bigger, of course, let your inner architect run wild, but the bed's the bare minimum we need to get started. Go on, hop to it. Get!
He disappeared after we got the lodestone working, vanished before you arrived. I'd like to track him down. To do that I need to cast a locator spell.

I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.
Hrmm?
Ah, hello there.

You've dealt with the problem for now, but who knows what danger waits around the corner? If I were you, I'd get yourself ready for whatever horribleness is coming next.
We can relax for a little while, but not forever. Velgar was one tough cookie, but he's just the foot soldier. Queen Kuldra is out there somewhere and she won't sit quietly for long.
Here, I'll take that rapidly decomposing head off you and give you something much better in return.
OK... not sure why you want to keep a decomposing dragon's head around, but you do you I guess.
I've got something to give you, but you've got your hands full. Go clear some space and then come back to me.

Keep your wits about you, young pup. Ashenfall is home to many a dangerous beast, and I've not yet tested my blade against each of them.
Getting ahead of yourself, aren't we, young pup? Check your map to see where you're meant to be headed.
My name is Vannaka and back on the mainland I was a Slayer Master. It was my job to send adventurers after dangerous beasts.
Be ready to fight, that's my first piece of advice. Craft armour, weapons and anything else you need for battle.
Well met, young pup. Looking to get yourself ready to face off against a dragon? You'll need more than that butter knife to kill one, but you've got to start somewhere.
Well met, young pup. Looking to get yourself ready to face off against a dragon? You'll need more than that potato masher to kill one, but you've got to start somewhere.
Cull the population of monsters, to make the world a better place.
There are goblins everywhere in Bramblemead and deadlier things beyond.
Well met, young pup. Seems your hunt was successful, I see you've gathered the food I asked for.
Well met, young pup. Seems like you haven't managed to cook that rat roast for me yet. You can get them by killing giant rats and cooking their meat. You can find some up by the windmill.
Look, you may have a weapon, but every great warrior knows wars are won by the stomach, not the blade.
I was finding things a little stale on the mainland. When I saw the posters for the expedition, I felt a pull... a call to adventure that I could not resist.
Past Bramblemead is Ghornfell, a place of danger and excitement. Something calls to me out there and I intend to seek it out.
It may not exactly be gourmet cooking, but a meal like this could make the difference between life and death. You'll not be taking on any dragons if you're starving to death.
Behind me, up that little hill, is a windmill infested with rats. I want you to kill some of them and cook their meat.
You will find rats are annoyingly resilient to clubs. Some enemies can resist certain damage types and be vulnerable to others.
Don't pull that face, you can't be a picky eater in a place like this. Food will make you healthier and heartier, and much more likely to survive.
Rats, for example, don't take kindly to getting stabbed. Here, take this little butterknife to make it easier to fight them in future. You can have this as well, it'll help you with what's next.
Properly cook a rat roast and bring them back to me. You'll probably burn a few along the way, don't let that disuade you. No one said survival would be pretty.
Right, let's teach you a bit about magic. Zanik's the one to talk to for that, you can find her down the road just before the river.
Hrmm, seems you're carrying the weight of the world right now. Come see me again when you've got some space free in your backpack.
Can you tell me about Ashenfall?
Who are you?
Welcome to Ashenfall, sorry about the mess. Had a bit of a dragon problem, that's why we've called for you.
You've come at a great time. Heroic opportunities await. This long-forgotten place is just screaming to be explored.
Strange place this. Ashenfall, I mean. Could make a real home here, if things stopped trying to kill us.
But before all that, how about we take you through some survival basics?
Gathering resources and crafting items, that's the basics of survival in this place. Seek out new resources to discover new recipes.
Oh dear, you just walked right past the Wise Old Man. He won't like that. Best go back and say hi, eh?
Me? Name's Doric. I'm just a stupid old blacksmith that got swept up in tales of adventure. Trying to win back me glory days.
It's a wild place this. Beasties everywhere, and no civilisation in sight. Just the remnants, ghosts of the past.
Left my son behind to watch the shop. Good lad, gonna do good things. Hope he's not too worried about his dad.

You'll want to get to grips with gathering and crafting first, Doric can help you with that.
Fair enough, I do like someone that can show initiative.
Ah, but you've got a good head on yer shoulders. I see you've already got some water, so you won't die of thirst.
Aye, that's a fine club you got there, but even the best weapons break over time. When that happens use a crafting bench to repair your gear.
Still, no point lollygagging around. I'll catch my breath and then explore these new lands. Who knows? Might find something.
You'll find him outside the temple. Check your map if you get lost, but he should be easy to spot.
But not here. Come find me in Bramblemead Village, and we'll get you started.
Still, it's going to be tough surviving this place with a dragon about.
By Saradomin's big bushy beard! Just our luck, a great ruddy dragon. Think it were him that got the others - may they rest in peace.
Ah good, you've got some water. Bit dirty, I know, but better than nothing. Be careful though, the water's tainted and it'll make life difficult if you drink too much.
Now you've got something to fight with, go chat to Vannaka over to the north east, he can teach you how to keep fighting fit.
Oh, you made a dagger, not a club? Aye, it's a nice piece of work, not what I asked for, but that's fine.
You'll want to build yourself a crafting table. Then once you've done that craft yourself a stone club.

And look at ya! Not a knife to yer name, no, no, we can't be doing with that. Come on, let's get you prepared. You need to go and craft a stone club.

Zanik says boiling it sorts it all out. So might want to give that a look later, when you've got a chance. Anyway, time we got you all set up to survive this harsh land.
I've marked two ponds on your map, to the northwest and south of us. Grab some water from there and bring it back here. Then I'll teach you what you'll need to survive.

Zanik says boiling it sorts it all out. So might want to give that a look later, when you've got a chance. Anyway, time we got you all set up to survive this harsh land.

objectives.text: Investigate the secrets hidden below Ashien's Watch.
Find someone near Ashien's Watch that can translate ancient dwarvish.
Bring the blueprint to Doric in Ashien's Watch.

dialogueRefs.text: The statue has no further secrets for you.
The door is sealed by Dragonkin magic.
A seal somewhere has broken.
The granite maul, now there's a weapon with heft. I wonder what other wonders the vaults are hiding?
How's the investigation going? I know Ashien's Watch must have something interesting to discover.
Oh, hello again. I'm impressed you've made it all the way out here. Really coming into your own, eh?
Oh, what's that? You found something? Let me take a look at that blueprint for you.
Oh, hello again. I'm impressed you've made it all the way out here. Really coming into your own, eh?

You see that place over there? Ashien's Watch they calls it. Used to be a site of some battle or other.

It's the sort of place where dragonkin would have hoarded their more interesting stuff. Feels like the sort of thing they'd do.
You find a weapon blueprint written in dwarvish. Perhaps Doric can help translate it.
Hrmm, this looks like a blueprint for a very special weapon, and look, I already found a bit to get you started!
I found a strange stone block covered in weird sigils, but then the garou ran me out of the place with threats of pointy sticks.
Ah, enjoy making that. These sorts of weapons are what an artisan lives for.

Best leave this alone for the moment.
Bwahahahahaha! Oh, hrmm? What do you want?

Graverobbing is a terrible hobby best left to necromancers and mad scientists.

You connect the body parts together like some terrible jigsaw puzzle. Your mother would be so proud.
Goblin legs, in a surprisingly good state. Goblin legs may look bandy and spindly, but they're surprisingly strong and would make a good foundation for this... creation.
The torso is muscular and well-preserved, perhaps the remains of a skilled warrior.

[PH] Cluck

You need lightning-in-a-bottle to power this machine.
Me? I was once-- no, I still am-- the most ingenius inventor of this and all other ages!

[PH] How is this possible - my calculations were....perfect
Bwahahahahahahahahaha...ahem... oh... hello. Who might you be then?
There are some small cuts and bruises across the legs, indication of some minor damaged sustained before the significantly more major damage that allowed you to find these legs in the first place.
Thin greenish veins run through the torso that generate an acrid smell. The signs of some sort of toxic corruption of the flesh.
Some of the muscles have deteriorated a little, as if the previous owner wasn't a focused fighter. Unusual for a garou.
[PH] You hear the pounding of the heart inside the Monster.

Doctor Victor Fenkenstrain!

[PH] Here not Igor, take these as a token of my thanks. It appears I have some calculations to do.

Excellent. Excellent! A somewhat motley collection of components, but we can work with it.
Now now, don't be squeamish, go give that body a poke would you? See what needs fixing with it.
Now, all you need to do, is get struck by lightning whilst holding that bottle I gave you. You'll be fine, don't grumble. Get shocked, then bring it back here and we shall continue our experiment!

Shockingly, you are able to capture the lightning in a bottle. You allow yourself to indulge in a single electricity based pun, and note that you should return to Doctor Fenkenstrain sooner rather than later.
Tragedies, yes, but tragedies that opened my eyes to my true destiny and the research that would consume my every waking moment..
Oh.You appear to be overloaded from your own scientific experiments. It's easy to get carried away. Return to me when you have some space free.

Some might call what we're doing ghoulish, but I prefer the term recycling. Reduce, reuse, recycle for a better future and all that.

WITH SCIENCE!

Quest_Heartstrings.description: Follow an elven bard's trail of memory, and discover a harmonious weapon.

objectives.text: Follow the memorial path, look for blue trees heading toward the east of Ghornfell and the memorial markers.

dialogueRefs.text: I never liked your story. Child of a farmer, given over to the Wild Knights, because of the fire in your eyes. It felt as if you were owed a greater story, one that could deliver even a fraction of your courage.

Gadael pob peth ar ôl    

Leaving everything behind, I thought only I did that.

We found a home here, together, the Wild Knight and her strange elf bard. We took the logs from the forests, and the stone from the mountain’s floor, so that we might craft a little place where we could escape together.

To an elf time is a fickle thing, we age so much slower that time passes almost without meaning. A year to us is a heartbeat, a decade is nothing but a brief rest, a century can be as easily forgotten as any other time. But not for you.
You didn’t die, you just went off to battle. That’s how I could brave the years. In the songs I wrote about you, you were off to war, fighting for Guthix against all the evils in creation.
You find a crystal in the shape of a seed. The memorial stone changes as you hold the crystal up, revealing text in elvish.
I laid your bones to rest beneath this tree, far from our home. I felt you deserved one last adventure, stretched out across our little world.
So I wrote this song to conjure up the essence of you, rather than the fact. A bard’s prerogative, evoke the feelings you left in others, rather than record your daily toils.

Wanderlust overcame reason and I journeyed across the ocean to find myself. Ashenfall is no place for an elf. There is no crystal, save what I brought with me, and the humans here distrust all outsiders. Not without reason.
I’m still not sure why we chose this land. Brynmoor was much calmer.

Every time you stepped out the door, it was as if time took some of you from me. In barely a handful of years your limbs stiffened, you fire-red hair turned grey and you lost some of the agility you had been so proud of.

Clwych curo’r drymiau rhyfel,  A ffanffer Guthix yn canu   

I imagined your war-song as you lead your Wild Knights into battle.

This view feels so different without you by my side. The angle is strange, because my shoulder isn’t weighed by your head as you lean on me and sigh softly. A hundred years without you, and yet this view still feels wrong.
This song was written for you... In memory of you. Yet the lump in my throat is so great, I cannot sound the words.
I laid your bones to rest beneath this tree, far from our home. I felt you deserved one last adventure, stretched out across our little world.

Er mwyn tynged Gilinor. Oh Gielinor  Mae’n daith un ffordd i fewn i’r affwys, i Gilinor   

That’s why you left me. Not the ravage of time. Not the cruelty of fire-red hair turning the silver-grey of burnt-out ash. You had a mission, a journey, to take the fight into the abyss.
Not you though. I remember sitting alone in the forests, wolves circling me, and then a loud crash, boisterous laughter and a mad-woman in leaf-covered armour falls out of a tree and says hello.

Y byd dirdro. Tir llygredig   

Ghornfell is a harsh place, filled with dangers. The land itself is twisted, poison to the east and storms to the west. Overhead the dread Velgar circles, laughing at the destruction he’s wrought.

Y pyrth hynaf,  
ar goll   

Those elder gates, stealing more of you from me.

Cleddyf guthix ydym ni  
Ni yw'r golau treiddgar  
Yr ydm yma
I drechu pob cysgod. I Gielinor!
It’s time for me to leave this place. To close this chapter on our memories and to start a life without you. I need to find myself again, without your shadow smiling out of the corner of my eye.
I'm sorry, Meya, even now I cannot say goodbye. So let me just say the words that mean the most.
This song was written for you... In memory of you. Yet the lump in my throat is so great, I cannot sound the words.

Trefn elitaidd rhyfelwyr affwysol   

Leaving me behind, so that you could save us all.

Marhog Gwagle! I Gielinor! 
Marchog Gwagle! Marchog! I Gielinor!   

A brave warrior, defender of the world. Defeated by a tree.

Creaduriaid. Adfeilion.   

Monsters and desolation, everywhere we looked. Yet somehow we made a home, a ramshackle house of nonsense, that became my paradise.
Yet, even as time left its wounds in your skin, you were still the most beautiful creature in all of Gielinor.

You were Guthix’s sword, his piercing light against the darkness. That’s why you left me. Not because of time. Not because you were never coming back. But because you needed to save us all from the monsters in the night.
I wrote a song about you, about the time we spent together. It’s a technique of my people, turning music into craft. I will play the pieces of it, as I take this goodbye walk.
Dw i'n dy garu di'n fawr.
I'm sorry, Meya, even now I cannot say goodbye. So let me just say the words that mean the most.
My journey continues eastward, following the blue in a sea made from waves of colourful dancing leaves. Saying my farewell, each footstep at a time.

We shared a meal. I told stories and you listened in a way that no one has ever listened before. All of you, every part of your being, focused on my words. I think I loved you even then, though it would be years before I realised it.

Y baradwys

Our world of adventure and excitement, held between four small walls.
A shield against a shadowy emptiness. My void knight.

I will start at our tree, in the east. Do you see it, down there, framed perfectly in this spot? A single point of brilliant blue, in an ocean of fiery red. An outsider, just like I was, until I met you.
Dw i'n dy garu di'n fawr.
As the last words leave your lips, the seed shivers and shudders to the song. It twists, stretches and transforms into a bow of glittering crystal.
You don't have enough space for the crystal seed to grow into the bow. You will need to make some room before it can do so.
Sing the bard's song of rememberance.
Step Away

I came to rebuild a farmstead. Now I'll serve as nothing but compost. Gran would be so upset with me.

He knew of this place, that dragon. Poked his great scaley head through the entrance and grinned at me as he slowly drew in a breath. I watched my life unfold before me, until the poison put it all to an end. I wish I'd found that shield.
Hurtling through the air, knowing everything was over. All I could think about was how I'd missed breakfast. Most important meal of the day, and I forgot it on my last one.

dialogueRefs.text: It's too dangerous to read this right now.
Black knights. I had hoped their special brand of madness was kept to the mainland, but here they are, even if they're not quite the knights I know.
What do you need, young pup?
You've got them all? Great, well done, young pup. Let's take a look at them then, see what sinister secrets they've learned...
Being nice to demons, what utter nonsense.
Nothing interesting happens
Nothing interesting happens
Nothing interesting happens
Three of them seem particularly dangerous, having learned how to bind demonic beasts to their service somehow.
Huh? Really? I was expecting dark rites, sinister spells and all that Zamorakian magic nonsense, but it's just...treating them nicely?
It's a hand written journal
It's a hand written journal
It's a hand written journal
Young pup, I need you to track these three down and bring me their training manuals. I want to know what cruelties they have unleashed on the beasts here.
According to the records here, his name was Walthar Skrexis. Kept mostly to himself, and had terrible hygiene habits.
From what I can tell, before the maddening corruption took him over, he was a knight called Philius Rexiton.
Lester Flament, is what the records say. Sounds like an odious person, unpopular even in a place like this.
I have a horrible feeling there's a metaphor there, but I'm too old and jaded to think about it. Here, you did what I asked, so I owe you something for your efforts.
Countless reports from the custodial team about how he would leave crumbs and bits of food everywhere, constantly attracting vermin.
Records seemed to indicate that he was a noble with a love for dogs. So it makes sense that he would try and wield the power of dog shaped demons.
Nowadays he's found wandering the crypts south of here, below the temple, with one eerily loyal demon.
This trinket should help you with all these demonic creatures. I don't think we have the time for the friendlier approach.
I love rats, they're so cute. What with their little whispers and their adorable inability to control their bladder.
I know they're just demons, but they're such good girls. I taught Gnasher how to sit, and Fido how to fetch.
I'm not sure if demon's even have birthdays, but I think I should get Delrom a cake. It's the polite thing to do.
Seems that he's still doing that, even with his mind turned to soup by this strange corruption madness.
He spends his time in the dungeons at the garisson, on the lower floors. There he seems to have gained the loyalty, or at least service, of a whole pack of hellhounds.
Young pup, I need you to track down three demon trainers, and bring me their journals. I want to know what cruelties they have unleashed on the beasts here.
I see you've got one of their training journals. Good work, young pup, but I need all three to unravel their techniques.
The tragedy being that they only live for such a short time. A year, maybe two. Barely a heartbeat.
Sure, Fido came back with a junior knight's still beating heart in her mouth, instead of the ball, but she's trying, bless her.
After all, they may be big, scary, and made of claws, but they might be the best friends I've ever had.
Seems he spends most of his times in the menagerie, south west of here.
But these hellrats? They live forever! An eternity of cute twitchy whiskers and fluffy little bellies in need of a scritch. What could be better?
All these mages and their complicated summoning and binding nonsense, and really all you need to do is throw them a decent steak every once in a while.
Oooh, I should make sure the cake has sprinkles!

Quest_SQ3_Nevermore.description: Investigate the strange corruption afflicting the residents of Dowdun Reach.

objectives.text: Speak to Zanik about the Corrupted Essence you got from a strange raven.
Gather 10 biological samples from strange ravens in Dowdun Reach, and bring them to Zanik.
Bring Zanik the ingredients. Dragons Blood. A Twilight Lily and some Unholy Water.
Find the source of the cthonian infection, somewhere high up in Dowdun Reach.
Return to Zanik and explain the situation.

dialogueRefs.text: Oh, hey, don't mind the cell, it's oddly comforting. I've been on the surface so long, I'd almost forgotten what it's like under the ground.
Oh, hey, don't mind the cell, it's oddly comforting. I've been on the surface so long, I'd almost forgotten what it's like under the ground.
I'm going to need: Some Dragon Blood, Unholy Water and the leaves of a Twilight Lily
Thanks again for helping figure out what was going on!
It's quieter here too, gives me time to think and look into stuff. This whole place, it's riddled with some sort of infection, or corruption, both magical and... well... more.
It's quieter here too, gives me time to think and look into stuff. This whole place, it's riddled with some sort of infection, or corruption, both magical and... well... more.
There is nothing of interest.
A cthonian demon... trapped in a chicken? Well that must be embarrassing. Still, you've got them to promise to reign in their infection and that means I can work on a cure.
If we can find that central intelligence, it would help in finding a cure down the line. Since ravens were infected most, maybe look for somewhere they frequent? Somewhere high up?
There is nothing of interest.
Hopefully we can keep that demonic corruption contained in Dowdun Reach...
I see you've already found the weird ravens and I'm sure you can see how weird they are right now.
There are ravens around this keep that are... stranger than the rest. More vibrant, a little luminescent.
Don't tell me you haven't seen the dragons roaming about? The blood of a dragon helps to add strength to the solution, unfortunately, you're going to need to kill one to get it.
Water that's been blessed by the priests of Zamorak. I'd look in the temple, maybe not everything there has been tainted?
The Twilight Lily, is a special flower that grows in damp dark places. I think I saw one by that tree in the lake further into the cave.
You've got them all. Great! May I take them?
It'll take a while though, years probably, but we might see this place recover over time. Thanks for all your help. Here, something to thank you for your effort.
If you can gather samples from, say... ten of them, I can maybe get a sense of what's been causing their strange behaviour. It might help me get to the bottom of the insanity in the keep.
You already have the Unholy Water.
Shouldn't be a problem for a strong adventurer like you right?
It's not much, but it's very fashionable in these parts.
You already have a leaf from the Lily.
Brilliant. Right, let's take a look at what we have here...hrmm...there's a lot of magical energy here, a bit like the dragonkin effigies we've seen...
Oh, right. Well I'll need them to continue. Let me know if you're ready to hand them over.
Fantastic! You've got enough there for me to study. I'm going to need a few more things, though, before I can learn anything from them. If you're still willing to help.
If you can gather ten samples from them, I can study them to see if I can unlock any clues as to the nature of the madness-infection in Dowdun Reach.
Wait... there's more than one infection here. One magical, one biological and distinctly demonic. Not avernic though, oh no, this is rare indeed.
Oh, you've got your hands full right now. Come back and see me when you've got some space free.
I need you to get me some reagents so I can study this corruption.
There's traces of cthonian demon here. See the way it wriggles? It's odd though, a bit like a parasite. It's part of a bigger whole though, there must be a central intelligence for it somewhere.
First, I'm going to need some dragon's blood. You can get it from any dragon you find, though I'm sure they won't be willing to surrender it without a fight.
If we can find that central intelligence, it would help in finding a cure down the line. Since ravens were infected most, maybe look for somewhere they frequent? Somewhere high up?
Then I'm going to need a twilight lily. They grow deep in the dark, by underground lakes. There's one not far from here.
Lastly I'm going to need some unholy water -- like holy water, only from Zamorak worshippers. There's probably a fountain somewhere near the Cathedral that has some.
Keep reagents
Hand over reagents
Ask about Unholy Water
Ask about Dragon Blood
Ask about Twilight Lily
If you bring me more of that essence you've found in the ravens, I'll give you some Infernal fragments for every ten essence you bring me.
Bwak?
Bwak?
I am Putriulius, grand-sub-sub-clerk of the great office of numerical records... which is to say that in the cthonian hierarchy, I was no one.
I am a cthonian demon. Once we were the rulers of Infernus, an existence of complex contracts and even more complicated culinary practices.
Must you call it an infection? You make me sound like a common cold!
My existence is just a joke to you, isn't it? Can you imagine what it is like for a being that has watched the rise and fall of civilisations... to be bound in such a feathery prison?
Bwaa-- oh it's you, I don't need to do the clucky thing. Oh, you've got some essence on you? Here, let me take it off your hands. Here you go.
Bwaa-- oh it's you, I don't need to do the clucky thing. What do you want? I've already agreed I'll do what I can to quell this infection.
I was small, quiet and easily forgotten, which goes a long way to explain why I wasn't eaten. I lived my life the blandest way imaginable, but I was happy in my own little way.
Which is to say that we ate one another. In doing so we gained strength, power, prestige, all the things a growing protean entity might need.
I had made myself small and split myself into hundreds of little versions of myself, and nestled myself inside what passes for brains in the avernic demons, later spreading to some of the humans.
If you were in my position, you would have gone mad long, long ago.
It's a surprisingly complicated language considering the source... oh... err... I mean, bwakbwak bwaaaak?
Um...yes, well... I mean... bwak!
No, very clearly I am a chicken... err, I mean... bwak bwak, cockadoodlesomethingorother.
I would love to, honestly I would. I got quite used to a life as little more than an observer, tagging along with the lesser demons.
When the rebellion happened, my people were destroyed in part by the very contracts we had created. Legal loopholes became the noose around our protoplasmic necks.
I could nudge, but couldn't control, so I lived myself, quite happily, as a spectator. Watching life from the safety of someone else's skull. That was until that big stone got smashed.
So, no, I do not have any eggs for you!
Urgh, I just can't do it anymore. How far from grace I have fallen to spend my aeons pretending to be a common farm fowl.
It was entertaining and I never needed to worry about being eaten by my fellow cthonians. But unfortunately the only part of me I can actually affect is.. well... this bit, in the chicken.

But I had an idea. Where the rest of my kind went big, I went small... very very small. Unbound as my kind are by your rather rigid notions of biology, I was able to split myself into little forms and crawled off to find my fortune.
With the energies that released, so too did something else. An ancient consciousness. Not strong enough to infect the minds of individuals, but my fractured parts were less able to defend themselves.
I would say I am part of this madness, yes, though I do not exactly claim credit for it. It was that... thing... that Dreaming Stone's mind that sent this wildly out of control.
I am Putrilius. Once one of the last remaining of the cthonian demons that were the rightful rulers of Infernus before it all went so very wrong.
Still, if you can get the Dreaming Stone under control, and its inhabitant can behave, I am willing to work to undo this nonsense. Though it might take some time.
Oh, but you're somewhat overburdened. Best come back when you've got some space free.
I nestled in, what you would call, the physical forms of the avernics and survived the great purge as a spectator, rather than a player. I lived, they died, so I call it a good plan.
What resulted is something like a civil war inside the flesh. Energies and consciousnesses ran rampant, warping and changing the hosts into what you see now.
When the war started I split myself up, into teeny tiny little versions of myself and hid myself, like a common parasite, in the lesser avernic demons. An excellent plan I thought, until I came here.
Look, tell you what. That essence you've been collecting, if you find any more of it, bring it back here. For every ten essences, I'll exchange you some of these Infernal fragments. Fair deal, no?
Frustratingly, I am largely unable to gain back control of the other bits of me, and now I am constrained to this feathered monstrosity.
If you find any more, I'll be happy to take it off your hands.

What are you?
Got any eggs I can have?

Bwak!
Can you end the corruption?

dialogueRefs.text: I'd be very happy if you could travel to Alcarrid, my camp in the south-east. It was my job to bring an envoy from other regions.
I don't know much about humans, but you don't look like a Black Knight. I guess I'll give the prepared speech anyway.
I'd be very happy if you could travel to Alcarrid, my camp in the south-east. It was my job to bring an envoy from other regions.
I COME HERE ON BEHALF OF THE MOON GAROU OF ALCARRID. WE SEEK AN ALLIANCE AGAINST THE DRAGON FUZAN.
So, not-a-Black-Knight, are you going to help us?
Well, that went better than I expected. You will need to travel south-east to Alcarrid, our camp, where your alliance will be processed.
That's...unfortunate. If and when you change your mind, come to my camp in Alcarrid and talk to the Elder.
And stay in the shadows as much as you can. The Umbral Sands is plagued by something called Scorch. The sun gives no leeway to unprepared humans.
I'm busy, I'm afraid
Sure, I will help you
Icthlarin, I am not disagreeing with you. But we are a young clan, only a few years old. We have barely learnt to survive in the desert. We aren't ready to confront a dragon!
Elder, with all respect, I am not asking you to face Fuzan. Leave that to me. I am merely asking for your clan's Mirror Lens.
And what then? You use this Mirror Relay to blast Fuzan's Volcano, and he flies here in a rage. We are not warriors! You cannot do that to my people.
You are the God of the Underworld. I know how this works. We couldn't stop you from taking our Mirror Lens. But please, earn the trust of my people before you condemn them.
Our clan is only a few years old, so we haven't had time to form our own myths or heroes.
Welcome to Alcarrid. I am afraid I am engaged as current, so please come back later.
We hoped we might be safer, moving further away from the dragon Fuzan. For a while that was true.
How are you finding the magic carpet? Beats getting sucked into quicksand, am I right?
I can't quite believe it: you have the trust and Mirror Lenses of Uzzer, Manafem AND Alcarrid? Not even Fuzan could bring the three clans together!
But you can bet that the gossips and storytellers of Alcarrid are going to claim you as one of their own!
But he has been making raids around the camp, and his KotHaar have been making demands of our goods.
Mallacht! My first year as an elder, and I'm stuck between a dragon and a demi-god.
Feel free to stay a while. The other clans are still reluctant to trade with us, so we could do with the business.
Now for the part that scares me to the marrow of my bones. I dearly hope you can slay Fuzan.
The Dragon Slayer of Alcarrid. A fine title.
But that doesn't mean that we can just take the fight to Fuzan. History tells us that resisting the dragons has not gone well.
As convincing as Icthlarin is, it will not be enough for my people. They will not just bow to his whims.
You are still a stranger to my people, human. Talk with them! I appreciate that they may be fearsome to your eyes, but they are anything but.
My people call you 'the one who watches'. It's better than 'the one who must be stabbed', I suppose. But you will need to help more if you want to earn their trust.
My people call you 'meddlesome', which loses something in translation, I suspect. It is a good thing! Keep helping!
One more task should do it! I have seen the younger garou copying the way you walk, your posture. It is a good sign!
You have earned the Alcarrid clan's trust. Our butcher has even named a new dish after you!
And there is more than just Fuzan to face in the Volcano. Make sure you are prepared, adventurer. It will be the greatest challenge you have faced.
My people do not trust the gods - that has gone badly for them. But you, adventurer: my Moon Garou could learn to trust you.
We have held council, and agreed to give you the clan's Mirror Lens. Ach, I hope we do not regret it.
Please, help my people with any tasks they may have. Only then will my people accept your request to hand over our Mirror Lens.
If you don't mind, I also wish to give you a personal gift. My partner is a weaver, and she has made you something.
Will you accept the burden that Icthlarin and I are placing on you?
It will bear you over quicksand. Navigating the sands will be a little easier.
Thank you, adventurer.  I am sure my people will make use of you.
We will wait. Be warned, though, Icthlarin does not like the patient sort.
Your very own magic carpet, blessed by Moon Sprites.
No doubt you will use it on your next step. If you wish to complete the Mirror Relay here, you will need the Mirror Lenses of Uzzer to the east, and Manafem to the south.
I have also persuaded our merchant to make more goods available to you. He was keeping the good stuff back from you.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
I'm busy, I'm afraid
Sure?
A human. How unbecoming. I hoped that we had moved far enough away from your sort.
Be off with you, Unmarked. Manafem lives are hard enough without prying human eyes.
A human. How unbecoming. I hoped that we had moved far enough away from your sort.
Go curry favours with your Alcarrid friends. You are not wanted here.
For all of our sakes, I hope you kill Fuzan. If you fail, then it is over. We are damned.
I do not give praise lightly, but you are remarkable. Killing Fuzan has lifted a great weight from the Uzzer, a weight that we did not know that we were carrying.
Be off with you, Unmarked. Manafem lives are hard enough without prying human eyes.
Do you not have an Alcarrid garou to pester? I can think of a million things I need to deal with more than you.
Fuzan's Mark burns more than ever. He has focused the Lens on us, I can feel it. Please - claim his head before he decides to claim us completely.
Sweet, blessed River Goddess, the pain of Fuzan's Mark has gone.
My scouts saw your approach, my advisers told me you were coming, and my seers predicted your arrival. I doubt a Kalphite Queen would make a greater noise.
You are a bad omen at a bad time, Unmarked.
It's like I am seeing the world afresh. My senses haven't been dulled by pain. Has the wind always made that whistling sound through our camp?
The Uzzer Clan are not the Alcarrid. We will not give up our Mirror Lens at the request of a half-god. Nor a human.
Oh, you are still here? I have heard whispers of your good deeds, but even those whispers are steeped in suspicion.
I know what you are doing. You are not selfless! This is all for the Mirror Lens. While my council pushes me to deal with you, I will not!
Could you complete your tasks a little quicker, and quieter, perhaps? And don't think that it will get you closer to my Mirror Lens.
My council urge me to listen to you. Do you not see how precarious my position is? While my council pressure me, I am the one who has to deal with Fuzan. I beg you - stop making my life harder.
We bear the Mark of Fuzan, and it is a wound that carves deep.
Are you struggling to earn our trust, Unmarked? It is not gained easily. We have been cheated so often that we expect it.
Thank you for helping that garou. But it will take more than that to win over my wary people.
I saw some labourers making jokes together! Do you know how rare that is? Keep going - I might even see one of them smile.
There is a phrase that our River Goddess taught us: 'to have a spring in your step'. That is how it feels to be a Manafem right now, Unmarked. Complete one more task and the Mirror Lens is yours.
Unmarked, I have more thanks than there are grains of sand in Umbral.
I have better things to do. I am preparing for Mark Day. It is the day we accept Fuzan's Mark on our body and, with it, his protection.
My council have voted to reduce my powers. I am overruled.
Please, stay a while in Uzzer. Our traders are unparalleled.
We may not look like we are bleeding, but each day we lose hope, sanity and fight. It pours and clots into the sand of Manafem.
Can I tell you something, Unmarked? Being a Manafem Elder is a punishment, not an honour. More garou turn it down than accept it.
You have a good heart, Unmarked. Manafem is lucky that you visited us.
And listen to me, calling you Unmarked! We are all Unmarked. Ah, the words feel so good in my mouth!
You have completed the tribe's tasks. Return to the Uzzer Elder
You have completed the tribe's tasks. Return to the Manafem Elder
Go help my people with things that they need doing. I will even be thankful for that. But I don't foresee me handing you our Mirror Lens.

As Elder, you must face Fuzan. You must meet his KotHaar envoys. Your Mark burns most when the clan fails him. And he is not easy to please...
Mark Day is cancelled. We will not submit to Fuzan.
For the first time, being Elder of the Manafem has been an honour. You have vindicated my choice to let you into Manafem. You have vindicated it tenfold.
And the Mirror Lens is yours. Please, understand the responsibility you are taking on. If you fail to defeat Fuzan, we die. All of us, to a whisker.
Take our Mirror Lens. Use it to burn a hole through Fuzan. Let the River Goddess's light pierce him.

I wish to talk to you, adventurer. But could you first visit the garou at the passage to Dowdun Reach? It would aid us both if she was returned safely.
When you're the guardian of the Underworld, the word 'Legacy' takes on an odd meaning.
I wish we could meet on better terms, adventurer. My name is Icthlarin, God of the Underworld.
You are really quite effective. The garou are looking at us with less than the traditional amount of disgust.
The dead fret about legacy. They worry about what they have left behind. I've never understood why. It means nothing to me.
Souls are coming to me from Umbral Sands at a faster and faster rate. My good friend Death informed me that the culprit is Fuzan, a dragon tyrant of these dunes.
Quite the busybody. You seem to have earned their trust. I would speak to the Elder.
Ugh, democracy is such a tiresome mortal concept. While we have convinced the Elder to hand over the Lens, it seems that we also have to convince his people.
The final two Mirror Lenses will be held by the remaining Moon Garou camps: Uzzer to the east and Manafem to the south.
The Mirror Relay...restored.
There is little time to waste, adventurer. We must repair the mirrors.
But the Moon Garou, Umbral Sands: this is my mother Elidinis's legacy. She nurtured something that was meant to grow. This place grew in her image, and it IS her, in so many ways.
It is time to push back, and there is no better weapon than this Mirror Relay. It is lacking three Mirror Lenses but, once complete, it could concentrate a light beam on Fuzan's Volcano.
This job suits you better than me. Earn Alcarrid's trust by completing tasks in the camp.

Your magic carpet will get a lot of use, I suspect. But that journey is for you, not me. I must stay here and guard the Mirrors. Fuzan will no doubt focus his efforts on them. They are the easier target.
But more importantly, Fuzan's Lens has been destroyed. It no longer provides protection around the Volcano. Fuzan is exposed.
I have positioned them carefully. I believe that they are directed towards Fuzan's Lens: the dragonkin relic which both protects his Volcano and powers Fuzan's Mark.
A formidable sight! I look forward to greeting Fuzan in the Underworld.
Would you be so good as to clear space in your inventory? I have something you might want.
We have preserved her legacy. And now I know what the word truly means. When the dead talk about what they left behind, I think I will understand a little better.
You have done so much good in these veiled lands. I beg you to do some more. Could you talk to the Alcarrid Elder, earn the trust of his people, and gain their Mirror Lens?
We must hurry. It is time to strike Fuzan before he retaliates. But I must warn you: he will use his KotHaar as a shield. You will likely need to face waves of them before confronting Fuzan.
That belief is about to be tested when you complete the Mirrors. Elidinis help me if I am wrong.
You, though - I hope to greet many years hence. Although, my intuition tells me that you will be facing Fuzan's mother next.
We would only need two more to complete the Relay. But it would be a mighty step towards slaying Fuzan!
Someone that foolhardy should go prepared. And to that end, I have a gift for you.
Part trophy, part defensive item, part Mirror Lens. I have put a fragment of my mother's mirror in there.

dialogueRefs.text: Delicious to view you, but Alcarrid Elder says that visitors must see him first.
Your meats have sold like hot snakes! My wares have never been hotter and more desirable.
Lovely human! It is tasty that you see me. It delects my eyes to see you.
I wait with breath bait! To remember, I want three raw farm meat, three kalphite shell fragments, and three cactus steaks from bunny cacti.
Human-tongue is not my first tongue. I am Moon Garou.
Raw farm meat come from raw mountain goats! They hop around on their hoofs near shady rock areas.

Cactus steaks come from bunny cactus. They have two big ears like a bunny! They're all about, but - if you feeling like you have green appendages - you could grow them instead.
There is no rush and I am patient. I am salted and pickled, so will not perish.
But enough funny chin-waggling! You will help me with task. I am slicer and server of flesh for garou. I am butch.
I smell your meats! Would you like to pass them to me?
Bring me three raw farm meat, three kalphite shell fragments, and three cactus steaks from bunny cacti. Speak to me again if you want some clue!
I never seen flesh so moist and juicy! You have eye for dead tissue and exoskeletons.
There is no rush and I am patient. I am salted and pickled, so will not perish.
I give you my succulent trust for making friends with Alcarrid.

I don't have any questions

dialogueRefs.text: I have furnished my shop with extra goods. It's my way of saying thanks for what you've done here.

No moonstones? Goodness, have I given you an impossible task? What a tragedy. Perhaps you should cross your fingers and mine gypsum deposits to the west.
You need the tribe's trust, and I'm its trader. I connect everyone here. Thus, you need my good word.
I can scarcely believe it! Moonstones don't exist! I thought I was leading you on an impossible chase, yet - well, here they are.
Now, don't take this the wrong way, but I had you followed. When you lost the moonstones, my partner re-acquired them. And what beauties they are.
Well, it won't come easy. I want three moonstones: a gem that I have never personally held in my hand. They are so rare, in fact, that most Moon Garou will tell you that they don't exist.
I am a Moon Garou of my word. You wanted my favour in trade for the moonstones, and I give it. My task is done. I shall also make my trading goods available to you.
Know this: I could have kept the moonstones and mentioned nothing to you. I did this as a favour. Someday, and that day may never come, I will call upon you to do a service for me.
If you want my help with the Elder, you better hope they are incorrect. My guess is that they are to the west, hidden in rocky areas or caves. Under gypsum, maybe.
