objectives.text: Bring Valas - The Blacksmith 3 adamant bars

dialogueRefs.text: You'll be wanting to talk to the Elder, not me.
The mirrors weren't just a symbol, you know. Back when this land was green and a lot less sandy, the River Goddess would use them.
You'll be the one who wants to remake the mirrors. Smells like folly to me, but I commend the spirit.
How she would use them, I don't know. A historian would tell you more than a blacksmith. But I like to think she reflected her power across the land.
Broken as they are, the mirrors are sacred to us. The River Goddess placed them here as a reminder of who must protect the Umbral Sands.
The job isn't a small one. It will need three adamant bars. If you've forgotten, the ore is found in various places to the south of here.
Right-ho, seems like you have the bars we need. If you don't mind, I'd like to do the work.
But before we can add the Mirror Lenses, we must fix their frames. As you can see, they are mangled.
The mirror will be fixed before you get the Lenses. I'll inform the Elder of your part in getting the job done. It was nice meeting you.
I've got other jobs I could be getting on with, you know.
Bring me three adamant bars to fix their frames. You can mine ore to make the bars at various mining spots to the south of here. You'll need to beware of kalphites, mind.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.

Quest_UmS_MainQuest1_TribeB_Task2.description: Dig up buried history in garou ruins far to the south

objectives.text: Dig up Forbidden Scrolls in the garou ruins. 0/4
Dig up Forbidden Scrolls in the garou ruins. 1/4
Dig up Forbidden Scrolls in the garou ruins. 2/4
Dig up Forbidden Scrolls in the garou ruins. 3/4
Return to Lehran - The Archaeologist in the Uzzer Camp

dialogueRefs.text: Would you like to know more about the texts you uncovered?
Oh no, no. There's a protocol in place for addressing the locals. You need to speak to the Elder first.
It is no secret that the schism was a defining moment for my people. The garou were once united under a single banner. We served under Lougrim, goddess of the moon.
Our people have always felt connected with the moon. There is something about its silver light that brings a sense of peace that's hard to describe to non-garou.
This Forbidden Scroll is fascinating. Our histories have reference of a Sun Demon, but they assume she arrived many thousands of years ago. But the Scrolls say that she arrives just after Fuzan.
To call it the Old Kingdom is perhaps a misnomer, for it is far more recent than our Ghornfell settlements. Nicer though... by a lot.
Not a problem! My mind is always available to you.
This Forbidden Scroll contains an alternate version of what really happened between Lougrim and Kuldra.
You have already found the ancient scroll that came from here.
This Forbidden Scroll shines a light on the real Moon and River Goddess.
You have already found the ancient scroll that came from here.
This Forbidden Scroll talks about the Sun Demon, but suggests she arrived reasonably recently.
You have already found the ancient scroll that came from here.
This Forbidden Scroll debunks the theory that ancient garou just disappeared in Umbral Sands.
You have already found the ancient scroll that came from here.

According to our traditions, we had the rite of challenge: anyone who could best the current monarch became ruler of the tribe. Lougrim challenged all the elders, becoming the High Queen of the Garou.
It's no surprise, then, that we favour deities of the moon. Our first was Lougrim, a goddess of the moon and of the hunt. She was slain by Kuldra. A dark time for our people.
The Scroll also says that she entrances people somehow, changing who they are and turning them into devout worshippers of the sun - sometimes of flame, depending on the story.
The Forbidden Scrolls confirm that the early Moon Garou were found travelling by a river goddess, who taught them culture and craft, so that they might move from settlements to cities.
Ah, you'll be the one that's looking for the Mirror Lens. A rare fragment of history, that.

Kuldra, the dragon queen and source of most of our problems, challenged Lougrim. Current garou history tells that this was a fair fight. Skill versus skill, might versus might. But according to the scroll, this was a lie!
Then, for a time, we wandered godless. We were alone, without the guidance we were so used to. That was until, one day, a child went missing in the sands.

She never seems to kill her victims. Indeed, the Forbidden Scroll implies that the subject lives a happy life in some sort of religious ecstasy. Their entire purpose in life is one of praise and adoration.
And these cities were giant. They had stone walls and colourful tapestries, dangling across streets to shield people from the sands.
How about we help each other out? Historian to historian. You help me learn the truth about my ancestors, and I vouch for you with the Elder.
The challenge wasn't issued at all! Lougrim had spent almost of all of her power shielding villages from dragonfire. Wounded and weak, Kuldra descended on her without mercy and simply devoured her.

She was found, resting in an oasis that hadn't been there until that day, listening to the song of someone beautiful. Our histories tell us she was a garou, but the Forbidden Scroll says that she looked more like a human!
Often those afflicted end up immolating themselves in some way. Horrifying, I know. They seek ways to burn themselves up, perhaps as some sort of sacrifice?
There were libraries filled with scrolls, full of the ancient words of our people. Festivals of colour, light, food and song.
How's the digging going? If you need a reminder of where you're heading, it's the ruins to the far south. Dripping with KotHaar they are.
This is fascinating, but it makes little sense to me without all four Forbidden Scrolls. Come back when you have them all.

There are some ruins far to the south, long lost to the sands. The KotHaar have stopped me from travelling there myself. It is said that beneath the sand are the Forbidden Scrolls. Four of them, in fact.

Kuldra declared herself queen and, out of fear, many garou followed her. But not us. Not those who would become Moon Garou. We refused to submit and fled our homes in search of a land free from Kuldra's cruelty.
Fascinating, yes? She called herself the goddess of the river, a moon deity that had left her old kingdom behind. In us she saw a people in need and she lifted us out of the dirt and into the dunes.
I suppose the moral is that curiosity must always be paired with caution, lest you might lose yourself in the discovery.
We put aside the need for the hunt, and found ways to enrich ourselves with art, sciences and magic. It was a golden age for my people.
The Forbidden Scrolls are said to contain the truth about the Moon Garou. Not what we have been fed by our Elders: what actually happened, many centuries ago.
I wonder why the truth of that moment was considered forbidden?
She taught us architecture and agriculture, and she gave us the mirrors to protect us from supernatural threats.

We were told that this civilisation became lost over time. But the scroll tells us it is a lie! Fuzan tore it down. He turned the very sun against us, so that we could no longer find comfort in the cities we had forged!
Goodness, I can see why they were called Forbidden Scrolls! So much of Moon Garou history is based on outright lies.
Dig them up, with a spade, bring them to me and you will have your recommendation. Sound fair? I'll even share the revelations, if there are any.

The Forbidden Scroll says that once she had helped us build our civilisation, she left this world for the stars - in search, perhaps, of some new souls in need of her guiding light. Can that really be the truth?
Luckily, there's nothing I like more than re-writing history books. This will keep me going for months!
She was not called El-Idahn-Inees, as our histories tell us. She was Elidinis: the mother of the Moon Garou.
I will petition the Elder to give you the Mirror Lens. And should you be curious, you can return to me and find out what was written in the Forbidden Scrolls.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
Ask about the Moon Goddess.
Ask about the Garou Schism.
Ask about the Sun Demon.
Ask about the Old Kingdom
Never mind.

Quest_UmS_MainQuest1_TribeB_Task3.description: Stop the Uzzer tribe from making a mistake and binding themselves to Fuzan's Mark

objectives.text: Convince the Uzzer councillors to abandon the Mark Day Festival. 0/3
Convince the Uzzer councillors to abandon the Mark Day Festival. 1/3
Convince the Uzzer councillors to abandon the Mark Day Festival. 2/3
Return to Shangruuh - Garou Envoy in the Uzzer Camp

dialogueRefs.text: The name's Alabrais. If you wish to discuss Mark Day, could we make it quick? I am a man of science, not a man of the people, and I have rocks to study.
I have already withdrawn my support for the festival. The others may still support it though.
The name's Brialka. I am a historian, and this - little human - is a Dragonkin Vault. Should you wish to discuss Mark Day, then I am more than happy to explain why I think it's best for our future.
I have already withdrawn my support for the festival. The others may still support it though.
Chirot's the name! Always happy to meet someone new, particularly if they have coin in their purse, or goods to fence. But why do I think you're here to talk about Mark Day rather than profit?
I have already withdrawn my support for the festival. The others may still support it though.
Good to see you. Go talk to the Uzzer Elder: you won't believe what they have to say for themselves.
Emotional, non-scientific nonsense. Who is to say that the Mark is equivalent to enslavement?
I always assumed the KotHaar worked for Fuzan voluntarily. But that assumption is unverified. Interesting.
An empty supposition. If Fuzan wanted us burned, we would be ash by now. Think scientifically, young one.
Let's not go overboard. I know many see me as an emotional historian, but I'm no fool. Fuzan hasn't burned us before, and he's unlikely to do it now.
Oh my, what a good point you make! I'm not just making a decision for the living, I am making it for - perhaps - multitudes more.
What do you mean by control? I'm sure Fuzan has better things to do than puppet an optimistic little historian from Uzzer!
Oh bravo, very dramatic. But drama won't make me rich, will it?
True, true. His raids have done a lot of damage to my business so far. But gaining Fuzan's protection will stop all that, won't it?
Oh boo hoo. There is always a hierarchy - people on the top, people on the bottom. Maybe you're just resentful that you're not on top, like me.
Best news I've heard all week! Not only has Fuzan Mark Day been cancelled, but the Elder's powers have been reduced! You're one step closer to the Mirror Lens.
A reasonable hypothesis. There are no data points where Fuzan has constructed systems or edifices, rather than taken control of them.
You certainly use imaginative imagery! But imagery has little value to a garou of science.
The world is a complicated place, young one. Like in geology, sometimes soft rock aligns with hard. I cannot agree with you.
You've done this debating thing before, haven't you? Yes, you are right - historically, the garou have been strongest together, and weakest apart.
I must stop you there! The Elder is strong-willed but trustworthy. Nothing in his history points to betrayal, and history is what I care about.
The young are so exciting to watch! But history tells me that open rebellion is more dangerous than any Mark Day.
A cut! A CUT! He wouldn't, would he? Well, I will just have to swindle more to make up for it.
Boring! Everyone can be bought. If anyone threatens me, I tuck some gems into their belt.
The most powerful rise to the top. They always do. There is plenty of room for Fuzan at the top and Chirot slightly underneath.
Why do the Uzzer garou have to be so insufferable? I came here to trade goods, but the Uzzer tribe are too busy planning for 'Fuzan Mark Day'.
There are three nobles on the Council, and you'll need to convince them all to drop the Fuzan Festival thing. They're all out in the wider region, putting their heads in the sands.
Promises almost never hold, young one. As a bond, it is one of the weakest. You will need a more scientifically proven argument than that.
You make a compelling argument. Both the KotHaar and the Mark show an orientation towards overbearing control. I will withdraw my support for the Mark Day.
Many garou will say they are miserable already! Things are relative, young one. You must consider proportional value in your scientific studies.
And have the blood of hundreds, perhaps thousands of garou on our hands? History would not be kind to us if that were the case.
Nothing brings people together like adversity. You are a convincing little human! You have my vote to cancel Mark Day.
If we dismantle governments every time a mistake is made, then how would we ever learn? History would repeat itself.
How can I NOT think about money? Coins have two sides: power and influence. I love them both.
You're right! Only Chirot gets to steal from his fellow garou! I am withdrawing my support for the festival. You can tell the Elder that I'm having none of it.
You misunderstand the mortal condition, my friend. There is always money to be made, ESPECIALLY when things are bad.
They don't know how terrible, awful and painful the Mark is! At any moment, Fuzan could decide to puppet our bodies. Nobody should willingly get the Mark.
That will be Alabrais. He's a geologist. You'll find him wherever there are big rocks, in the direction of Fuzan's Volcano. He's a garou of logic, and his love is for science.
That's Brialka, the historian. He'll be outside the Pyramid, north of here. He is the emotional type, loves his history, and will do anything to ensure a legacy for his people.
Ugh, Chirot. He's a glorified graverobber, stealing treasures from the desert. He is as selfish as they get, only concerned about his wealth and interests. You'll find his camp to the south of here.
Well, good luck all the same.
The Elder won't change their mind, but the Council might. Please, find Uzzer's councillors near the landmarks of this region. Persuade them that Fuzan Mark Day is the most terrible of terrible ideas.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
You will need to pay attention to what the councillors value. I know a little about each of them, if you are interested?
That will be Alabrais. He's a geologist. You'll find him wherever there are big rocks, in the direction of Fuzan's Volcano. He's a garou of logic, and his love is for science.
That will be Alabrais. He's a geologist. You'll find him wherever there are big rocks, in the direction of Fuzan's Volcano. He's a garou of logic, and his love is for science.
Ugh, Chirot. He's a glorified graverobber, stealing treasures from the desert. He is as selfish as they get, only concerned about his wealth and interests. You'll find his camp to the south of here.
Well, good luck all the same.

Quest_UmS_MainQuest1_TribeC_Task1.description: Follow the trail of the Dearg Due to the south, and retrieve the body of its victim.

objectives.text: Track down the Dearg Due through the sandstorm
Give Efina - The Lost some clean water
Return to Manathep - The Bereaved

dialogueRefs.text: I'm beside myself! Please, talk to the Elder then come back to me after. I have need of you.
Don't worry, I'm safe and healthy. I'm just making the hardest choice of my life.
Efina's alive? Efina's alive! Glory upon the River Goddess!
I am so lost... the sand it... it obscured everything.  Water, please, do you have any clean water?
The Dearg Due! The Dearg Due! It killed my poor Efina!
Please, we will get no peace until the Dearg Due is dead. It watches us from the south of the camp. Kill it, then find my Efina's remains.
Well, if the beast didn't kill Efina, then it must have tricked her. Efina wouldn't go into the desert alone.
I can feel the strength coming back to me. Thank you.
Have mercy, I'll die without water. Please help.
I am so lost... the sand it... it obscured everything.  Water, please, do you have any clean water?
Efina was taken three days ago, and every night the Dearg Due has been watching me from the south of the camp with a glint in her eye and blood on her lips. She be gloating!
I can barely wait for my Efina to come back. And don't you worry - I'll tell the Elder all about what you done for me.
I ran away from Manafem. I couldn't do it any more: the Mark, the overbearing sadness, my mum keeping watch over me every waking hour.
Have mercy, I'll die without water. Please help.
The Dearg Due is a wicked beast. Lures you into the sands then snaps your bones. Oh, Efina!
Tell mum that I'm safe, that I'm on my way back. It may be the truth, it may not. I have a decision to make.
You have to kill it! Kill the Dearg Due! Go south where it prowls, an' make sure it never kills another. Then, please, bring back my Efina's body.
Whichever way I am heading - thank you. And thanks to you, Dearg Due. I was brought up to fear you, but I know now that was wrong.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
The Dearg Due howls.
You get the sense that a curse has been lifted and the Dearg Due can move on from this world.
Give water
Don't offer it yet

Quest_UmS_MainQuest1_TribeC_Task2.description: Find some lost garou scouts and slay the creature they have been tracking

objectives.text: Locate the dragon to the east and bring its heart back to Hedric - The Hunter
Search the village to the east for signs of the lost scouts

dialogueRefs.text: Move along, human. Head to the Elder if you plan on sticking around.
This must be one of Hedric's lost scouts. The poor garou has been torched completely.
A garou lies here, twisted in agony and burned.
A garou lies here, its fur matted with blood. There is something large and white embedded in its back.
A garou lies dead here, covered in blood.
The ruins have been charred by a concentrated blast of fire. The Scorch and sandstorms could not have done this.
The bricks here have been charred by fire.
We have one fewer thing to fear. Thank you.
There are no blades or arrows here. The corpse reeks of the familiar smell of sulphur.
It's a tooth. An extremely large tooth.
While large, the blast is lesser than that of Fuzan. Whatever did this is smaller, but not that much smaller.
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
Move along, human. Head to the Elder if you plan on sticking around.
There are always two kinds of people: the weak and the vultures. When someone is down, needing help, there's someone like you - hovering, waiting to pick from the carcass.
You want to prove that you're not? Hmmm. Well, my latest scouting party have gone missing, on the trail of a creature that has been picking off my people, one by one.
A dragon! Of course it's a dragon. We'll just throw it on the pile with the sandstorms, Fuzan, kalphite and KotHaar.
Thank you for finding my scout's bodies. I feared that would be the case. I will send someone to bury them, now that you have made the area safe.
You killed the creature already? If it was a dragon of that size, I fear my scouts are dead. The Manafem are strong, but not that strong.
Find my scouts, then help them track down the beast. Bring me its heart - if it has one. Do that, and I might think twice about you. They should be somewhere off to the east.
My request hasn't changed. Kill it. The people of Manafem will be much obliged.
Must I repeat myself? Find my scouts to the east, and help them to track the beast then take its heart. I'm confident they are somewhere to the east.
Still, that dragon will have been small-fry compared to Fuzan. I hope you know what you're doing. Regardless, I have given my recommendation to the Elder.

Quest_UmS_MainQuest1_TribeC_Task3.description: Complete the lost 'Song of the Ancients' by finding lyrics within the Dragonkin Vault.

Transcribe lyrics written on statues within the Dragonkin Vault. 1/3
Transcribe lyrics written on statues within the Dragonkin Vault. 2/3
Return to Laguna - The Bard in the Manafem Camp.

dialogueRefs.text: We have much to talk about, but everyone is staring. I think you need to visit the Elder before we discuss.
Words are inscribed on the statue.
A statue with Garou inscriptions.
Words are inscribed on the statue.
A statue with Garou inscriptions.
Words are inscribed on the statue.
A statue with Garou inscriptions.
It's time to move on, I feel. I wonder if the Alcarrid tribe are more my vibe.

"Five cradles stood empty on that baleful night,
A monster claimed them, and then took flight.
It left no footprints or scent on the air,
All the garou could follow was a thread of despair."

"A shaman journeyed on the garous’ behalf.
Moon sprites twinkling on his adamant staff.
Kalphite skittered with a twist of his wrist.
Till the monster approached. “Shaman, desist.” "

“A staff will not kill me. Ha - it’ll take more than that!
I have something to trade for your five little cats.
Their young minds are worthless. I need something older.
I’ll take what’s in your hand, and what's on your shoulder.”
Please, make space in your inventory so I can give you what I owe you.
You've found them all! Deeeelightful. Let me weave them into verse.
Where did I send you again? Oh yes: head south to the Vault and look for lyrics carved into statues. Just watch out for beetles!
Oh. That's... tragic. I imagined a more heroic fate than that.
You have already transcribed these lyrics.
You have already transcribed these lyrics.
You have already transcribed these lyrics.
Is it a mirage? A wondrous warrior has stepped in from the desert. My name is Laguna: the finest travelling bard this side of Kuldra's Tower.
If it isn't the Dreamboat of the Desert! The ancient saga we recovered together has been getting me a lot of attention. And I mean a LOT.
It does make me wonder. Perhaps I am not descended from the shaman, and am - instead - descended from one of the children he saved.
I need your help with something, if you would. My great-great-grandfather was a shaman, and I came here to learn more about him. Perhaps write a song in his honour.
Sigh. I guess I will never know. I'm not sure what good it will do you, but I will vouch for you to the Manafem Elder.
But the Manafem garou are less than helpful. They say 'everything I need to know is in the Vault'.
They say that his children wrote a song about him? It's inscribed onto three statues within a pyramid-like vault, somewhere to the south.
Would you go there and write down the lyrics on the statues? I would go myself, but it's said that there are beetles in the vault. And you know... ick.
That's it! The Song of the Ancients is complete. Laguna - The Bard will want to hear the complete verse.

Quest_UmS_Vannaka.description: [PH] Vannaka is fascinated by the Kalphite. Help him understand them more.

objectives.text: [PH] Bring a Kalphite shell to Vannaka to study
[PH] Bring a Kalphite wing back to Vannaka for him to study
[PH] Bring some Kalphite ichor back to Vannaka

dialogueRefs.text: [PH] Ah - just the person I was hoping to see.
[PH] Thank you for all your help pup.
[PH] I’ve been hearing strange things from the sands. Kalphites… but not as we know them. Creatures like that demand understanding - not guesswork, Pup.
[PH] I’ll admit it plainly; this is unfamiliar ground for me. If I’m to teach others how to face them, I need to study them up close.
[PH] Ah… that’ll be the wing, then. Let me see it.
[PH] Back again, but I see no wing.
[PH] Ah! You’ve returned! And with… Kalphite Ichor? Incredible!
[PH] Pup, we need Ichor to learn what drives these creatures.
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
[PH] Back already? Hm. I take it you didn’t manage to bring back a shell.
So, what do you say to helping me out a bit more?
[PH] By Guthix, you actually brought one.
[PH] Interesting… far too dense for flight. No, this isn’t for the air; it’s built for balance, for sudden shifts in movement beneath the sand.
[PH] If we’re to understand how these Kalphites move, I’ll need more than the shell alone.
[PH] I can feel its essence just by holding this. This will be invaluable in understanding how these creatures operate. With this, I feel far more prepared for dealing with the Kalphite threat.
[PH] I see. Not a task to take lightly, I suppose.
[PH] Bring me an intact Kalphite shell, and you’ll be doing more than helping me, you’ll be sharpening every Slayer’s edge.
[PH] No matter, but without it, I’ve nothing to study. The Kalphites of the Umbral Sands won’t reveal their secrets so easily.
[PH] I see. Not a task to take lightly, I suppose.
[PH] Bring me an intact Kalphite shell, and you’ll be doing more than helping me, you’ll be sharpening every Slayer’s edge.

[PH] Feel this… layered chitin, thicker than I expected. Not just armour, this is grown to deflect, to absorb impact. Blades would glance off if you don’t strike with purpose… right along these seams.
[PH] See here? Reinforced channels. Likely used to sense vibrations… or to stabilise them when they lunge. A Slayer who ignores these would be caught off guard.
[PH] Bring me a wing, Pup, and we’ll finish what we started.

[PH] Truly, your help has made a difference. Take this token of my appreciation, it should aid you in your travels, and perhaps give you a little edge if you cross paths with these foul insects again.
[PH] Return when you have one. Fragments will not suffice.
[PH] “Wait… is that? By Guthix! You already have one.
[PH] A Slayer’s approach, then; precision over force. Break the structure, not the shell. Hm… fascinating.
[PH] Shell for defence. Wings for control… which leaves one final piece.
[PH] Once more, thank you. You’ve done more than I could have asked for.

[PH] Feel this… layered chitin, thicker than I expected. Not just armour, this is grown to deflect, to absorb impact. Blades would glance off if you don’t strike with purpose… right along these seams.
[PH] But this raises another question. If their shells have adapted… what of their mobility?
[PH] I need to see its ichor, the blood. Bring me that, and we’ll learn what truly drives these creatures… and how to bring them down for good.
[PH] A Slayer’s approach, then; precision over force. Break the structure, not the shell. Hm… fascinating.
[PH] I need a Kalphite wing. Bring me one, and we’ll see how these creatures move—and more importantly, how to stop them.
I've got something for you, a thank you of sorts, but you're a little overburdened. Clear out some of that backpack and then come back and see me.
If it's anything like the bow, it'll be stored in a vault somewhere. Can you bring it to me? It'll really help with my research.
I'm listening
Maybe later
I'm listening
Maybe later
The statue has no further secrets for you.
The statue has no further secrets for you.
Your mind fills with the knowledge of a new crafting recipe... but at what cost?
The statue's shadow seems to shiver as though giggling with wicked malice. A tendril of night touches you and your mind fills with the knowledge of how to craft a weapon of unnatural power.
You lack the trophy the shadow desires. It waits silently for you to bring it what it seeks. Your mind fills with images of flickering purple lightning, and arms like blades.
